translations.idiomatic: ○ Song Bai · Liang Zhouhan · Zhu Ang · Zhao Linji

sentences.zh: 宋白，字太素，大名人。

translations.literal: Song Bai, styled Taisu, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Song Bai, courtesy name Taisu, was from Daming.

sentences.zh: 年十三，善屬文。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, he was skilled at composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he could already compose polished prose.

sentences.zh: 多遊鄠、杜間，嘗館於張瓊家，瓊武人，賞白有才，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: He often wandered between E and Du, and once lodged at Zhang Qiong's home; Qiong was a military man who appreciated Bai's talent and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: He often traveled between E and Du and once lodged with Zhang Qiong, a military officer who admired his talent and treated him with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 白豪俊，尚氣節，重交友，在詞場中稱甚著。

translations.literal: Bai was bold and distinguished, valued integrity and spirit, prized friendship, and was highly renowned in literary circles.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and spirited, he prized integrity and friendship alike, and enjoyed wide renown among men of letters.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，竇儀典貢部，擢進士甲科。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, Dou Yi presided over the examination bureau; Bai was selected as a jinshi of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 961 Dou Yi oversaw the civil examinations and Song Bai passed among the top tier of jinshi.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，獻文百軸，試拔萃高等，解褐授著作佐郎，廷賜襲衣、犀帶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, he submitted one hundred scrolls of writings, passed the special selection examination with high standing, was granted office upon leaving the common cloth and appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat, and was given court robes and a rhinoceros-horn belt at audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qiande era he submitted a hundred scrolls of writings, placed at the top of the special selection examination, entered service as a Secretariat assistant gentleman, and received court robes and a rhinoceros-horn belt in audience.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，授玉津縣令。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was appointed Magistrate of Yujin County.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Shu he was made magistrate of Yujin County.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，閻丕、王洞交薦其才，宜預朝列。

translations.literal: During the Kaibao period, Yan Pi and Wang Dong repeatedly recommended his talent, saying he should participate in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao years Yan Pi and Wang Dong repeatedly recommended him for court office, arguing that his talents deserved a place in the central government.

sentences.zh: 白以親老祈外任，連知蒲城、衛南二縣。

translations.literal: Bai, citing his elderly parents, requested an outer appointment and served successively as magistrate of Pucheng and Weinan Counties.
translations.idiomatic: Citing aged parents at home, he sought a provincial post and served in succession as magistrate of Pucheng and Weinan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，與程羽同知貢舉，俄充史館修撰、判館事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, together with Cheng Yu he oversaw the examinations; soon he served as Compiler in the Historiography Institute and concurrently directed its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 980 he and Cheng Yu jointly supervised the civil examinations, and shortly thereafter became a compiler in the Historiography Institute with charge of its daily administration.

sentences.zh: 八年，復典貢部，改集賢殿直學士、判院事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again presided over the examination bureau, and was transferred to the title of Academician Recruit of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the institute's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 983 he again headed the examinations and was made Academician Recruit of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the institute.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as Academic Laureate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academic laureate.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，召白與李昉集諸文士纂《文苑英華》一千卷。

translations.literal: During the Yongxi period, Bai was summoned with Li Fang to gather various literary men to compile the Wenyuan Yinghua in one thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi years he and Li Fang were charged with assembling scholars to compile the thousand-scroll Wenyuan Yinghua anthology.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，加禮部侍郎，又知貢舉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Rites, and again oversaw the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong era he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and again put in charge of the examinations.

sentences.zh: 白凡三掌貢士，頗致譏議，然所得士如蘇易簡、王禹偁、胡宿、李宗諤輩，皆其人也。

translations.literal: Bai thrice presided over the selection of examination candidates and drew considerable criticism, yet the scholars he obtained, such as Su Yijian, Wang Yucheng, Hu Su, Li Zong'e, and their kind, were all his selections.
translations.idiomatic: Song Bai presided over the examinations three times and drew considerable criticism for it, yet the scholars he advanced—including Su Yijian, Wang Yucheng, Hu Su, and Li Zong'e—were men of genuine merit.

sentences.zh: 是時，命復舊制，專委有司，白所取二十八人，罷退既眾，群議囂然。

translations.literal: At that time an order restored the old system and entrusted the matter exclusively to the proper officials; of the twenty-eight persons Bai had selected, very many were dismissed, and public discussion became clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court restored the old examination procedures and entrusted selection to the regular officials alone; of the twenty-eight candidates Bai had passed, a great many were failed, and public outrage was loud.

sentences.zh: 太宗遽召已黜者臨軒覆試，連放馬國祥、葉齊等八百餘人焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong hastily summoned those already failed for a reexamination before the throne and in succession passed over eight hundred persons, including Ma Guoxiang and Ye Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong promptly ordered the failed candidates to a palace reexamination and passed more than eight hundred of them in succession, including Ma Guoxiang and Ye Qi.

sentences.zh: 白嘗過何承矩家，方陳倡優飲宴。

translations.literal: Bai once passed by He Chengju's home when singers and entertainers were being displayed in drinking and feasting.
translations.idiomatic: Song Bai once called on He Chengju's home while singers and entertainers were being displayed at a feast.

sentences.zh: 有進士趙慶者，素無行檢，遊承矩之門，因潛出拜白，求為薦名，及掌貢部，慶遂獲薦，人多指以為辭。

translations.literal: There was a jinshi candidate named Zhao Qing who by nature lacked moral restraint and frequented Chengju's household; he secretly came out to pay respects to Bai and asked to be recommended by name, and when Bai presided over the examination bureau, Qing indeed obtained recommendation—many pointed to this as grounds for criticism.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi candidate named Zhao Qing, a man of poor character who frequented He Chengju's household, slipped out to pay his respects and ask for a recommendation; when Bai later headed the examinations, Qing was passed—and many cited this as evidence against him.

sentences.zh: 又女弟適王沔，淳化二年，沔罷參知政事。

translations.literal: Moreover, his younger sister by a different mother was married to Wang Yan; in the second year of Chunhua Yan was dismissed from his post as Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger half-sister was married to Wang Yan, who lost his post as Vice Grand Councilor in 991.

sentences.zh: 時寇準方詆訐求進，故沔被出，復言白家用黃金器蓋舉人所賂，其實白嘗奉詔撰錢惟濬碑，得塗金器爾。

translations.literal: At that time Kou Zhun was slandering others to advance himself, and therefore Yan was removed; he again said Bai's household used gold vessels that were bribes from examination candidates, but in truth Bai had once been ordered to compose the stele inscription for Qian Weijun and had received gilt vessels for that.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was then slandering rivals to advance himself, and Wang Yan's removal was part of that; Yan also claimed that gold vessels in Bai's household were bribes from examination candidates—in fact they were gilt pieces Bai had received for composing a memorial stele for Qian Weijun at imperial order.

sentences.zh: 先是，白獻擬陸贄《榜子集》，上察其意，欲求任用，遂命知開封府以試之，既而白倦於聽斷，求罷任。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bai had submitted a work modeled on Lu Zan's Bangzi Collection; the emperor perceived his intention and desired to employ him, and therefore ordered him to govern the Kaifeng Prefecture as a trial; before long Bai grew weary of hearing cases and requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bai had submitted a work modeled on Lu Zan's Bangzi Collection; the emperor saw his ambition for office and appointed him prefect of Kaifeng as a trial, but Bai soon tired of hearing lawsuits and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，擢王欽若、馮拯、陳堯叟入掌機要，以白宿舊，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, Wang Qinruo, Feng Zheng, and Chen Yaosu were promoted to manage state secrets; because Bai was a longtime official, he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1001 Wang Qinruo, Feng Zheng, and Chen Yaosu were elevated to the inner councils of state; Song Bai, as a senior figure of long service, was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 白學問宏博，屬文敏贍，然辭意放蕩，少法度。

translations.literal: Bai's learning was broad and abundant, and his composition was swift and rich, yet his diction and meaning were unrestrained and he observed little propriety.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was vast and his prose swift and fluent, yet his style ran to extravagance and he showed little regard for decorum.

sentences.zh: 在內署久，頗厭番直，草辭疏略，多不愜旨。

translations.literal: Having long been in the inner secretariat, he greatly wearied of rotation duty; his draft edicts were cursory and often did not satisfy the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in the inner secretariat he wearied of rotating duty there; his draft edicts grew perfunctory and often missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，與梁周翰俱罷，拜刑部尚書、集賢院學士、判院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, together with Liang Zhouhan he was dismissed from the Hanlin, and was appointed Minister of Justice, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and given charge of the institute's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1005 he and Liang Zhouhan were both dismissed from the Hanlin Academy; Song Bai was made Minister of Justice, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and given charge of that institute.

sentences.zh: 舊三館學士止五日內殿起居，會錢易上言，悉令赴外朝。

translations.literal: Formerly, academics of the Three Repositories were required to attend only at the inner court on the fifth day; when Qian Yi submitted a memorial, all were ordered to attend the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Three Repositories academicians need only attend the inner-court audience on the fifth of each month; when Qian Yi memorialized on the point, the court ordered them all to join the outer-court assembly.

sentences.zh: 白羸老步梗，就班足跌。

translations.literal: Bai was frail and elderly with stiff gait; when he took his place in the ranks his foot stumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Frail and elderly, with a stiff and stumbling gait, he tripped when taking his place in the outer-court ranks.

sentences.zh: 未幾，抗表引年。

translations.literal: Before long he submitted a memorial citing age to request retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he submitted a memorial pleading age to request retirement.

sentences.zh: 上以舊臣，眷顧未允。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he was an old minister, showed him favor and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, cherishing an old servant, refused the request.

sentences.zh: 再上表辭，乃以兵部尚書致仕，因就宰臣訪問其資產，虞其匱乏，時白繼母尚無恙，上東封，白肩與辭於北苑，召對久之，進吏部尚書，賜帛五十匹。

translations.literal: When he again submitted a memorial requesting leave, he was permitted to retire with the title Minister of War; the emperor then asked the chief councilors about his assets, fearing him destitute; at that time Bai's stepmother was still in good health; when the emperor went east for the feng sacrifice, Bai shouldered a burden and took leave at the Northern Park; summoned for a long audience, he was advanced to Minister of the Civil Office and granted fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted again, he was allowed to retire as Minister of War; the emperor had the chief ministers inquire into his means, fearing he might be in want. His stepmother was still alive. When the emperor traveled east for the feng sacrifice, Bai took leave of him at the Northern Park shouldering a pack; the emperor summoned him for a long audience, promoted him to Minister of the Civil Office, and granted fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，丁內艱。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he observed mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1010 he entered mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, he died at age seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1012 he died at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射，錄其孫懿孫為將作監主簿，孝孫試秘書省校書郎，從子唐臣試正字。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his grandson Yisun was entered as Principal Clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, Xiaosun was tried as Proofreader of the Secretariat, and his nephew Tangchen was tried as Regular Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his grandson Yisun was appointed principal clerk in the Directorate of Palace Buildings, Xiaosun was given a probationary post as Secretariat proofreader, and his nephew Tangchen as probationary regular scribe.

sentences.zh: 白善談謔，不拘小節，贍濟親族，撫恤孤藐，世稱其雍睦。

translations.literal: Bai was skilled at jest and banter, did not constrain himself in small matters, supported and aided his kin, and comforted the orphaned and young; the age praised his harmonious kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of wit and banter and cared little for small formalities, yet he supported his kinsmen generously and tenderly raised orphans and the young—the age praised the harmony of his household.

sentences.zh: 聚書數萬卷，圖畫亦多奇古者。

translations.literal: He amassed tens of thousands of scrolls of books, and his paintings too included many rare and antique pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He collected tens of thousands of books, and his gallery held many rare and ancient paintings.

sentences.zh: 嘗類故事千餘門，號《建章集》。

translations.literal: He once classified over a thousand categories of precedents, which he titled the Jianzhang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He once classified more than a thousand categories of institutional precedents in a work titled the Jianzhang Collection.

sentences.zh: 唐賢編集遺落者，白多纘綴之。

translations.literal: Where Tang worthies' compilations had omissions, Bai often gathered and joined them together.
translations.idiomatic: Where Tang anthologies had left pieces out, he often gathered and restored them.

sentences.zh: 後進之有文藝者，必極意稱獎，時彥多宗之，如胡旦、田錫，皆出其門下。

translations.literal: Toward juniors possessing literary talent he always praised them to the utmost; contemporary outstanding men mostly looked to him as master, such as Hu Dan and Tian Xi, who were all under his tutelage.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished praise on talented juniors, and many leading men of the age took him as their model—Hu Dan and Tian Xi among others came up under his wing.

sentences.zh: 陳彭年舉進士，輕俊喜嘲謗，白惡其為人，黜落之，彭年憾焉，後居近侍，為貢舉條製，多所關防，蓋為白設也。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian took the jinshi examination; he was frivolous and clever and fond of mockery and slander; Bai detested his character and failed him; Pengnian resented this; later holding a post close to the emperor, when making examination regulations he added many restrictions—it was evidently aimed at Bai.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Pengnian sat for the jinshi examinations, Bai failed him on account of his frivolous and sarcastic character; Pengnian never forgot the slight. Later, as a palace attendant, he drafted examination regulations bristling with new restrictions—aimed largely at Song Bai.

sentences.zh: 會有司諡白為文憲，內出密奏言白素無檢操，遂改文安。

translations.literal: When the proper offices were about to bestow on Bai the posthumous title Wenxian, a secret memorial issued from within said Bai by nature lacked restraint in conduct, and it was changed to Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was about to grant him the posthumous title Wenxian, a secret memorial from within the palace objected that he had never shown self-restraint, and the title was changed to Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 有集百卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in one hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to a hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子憲臣，國子博士；

translations.literal: His son Xianchen was a Doctor of the Imperial Academy;
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianchen served as a doctor of the Imperial Academy;

sentences.zh: 得臣，賜進士及第，至太常丞；

translations.literal: Dechen, granted jinshi status with highest honors, rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Dechen received jinshi honors by imperial grant and rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 良臣，為太子中舍；

translations.literal: Liangchen served as Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen served as Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 忠臣，殿中丞。

translations.literal: Zhongchen was a Palace Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen served as a palace aide.

sentences.zh: 梁周翰，字元褒，鄭州管城人。

translations.literal: Liang Zhouhan, styled Yuanbao, was a native of Guancheng in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhouhan, courtesy name Yuanbao, was from Guancheng in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父彥溫，廷州馬步軍都校。

translations.literal: His father Yanwen was Commander-in-Chief of the Infantry and Cavalry of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanwen was commander of infantry and cavalry at Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周翰幼好學，十歲能屬詞。

translations.literal: Zhouhan from youth loved learning, and at ten could compose verse.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning, and at ten he could already compose verse.

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年舉進士，授虞城主簿，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Chief Clerk of Yucheng, but declined citing illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In 952 he passed the jinshi examinations and was appointed chief clerk of Yucheng, but pleaded illness and declined the post.

sentences.zh: 宰相範質、王溥以其聞人，不當佐外邑，改開封府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Chancellors Fan Zhi and Wang Pu, because he was a man of renown, said he should not assist an outer district and transferred him to Army Master of the Household Section of the Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Fan Zhi and Wang Pu, reckoning a man of his stature unsuited to a county post, moved him to Army Master of the Household Section in the Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋初，質、溥仍為相，引為秘書郎、直史館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, Zhi and Pu still served as chancellors and recommended him as Secretariat Gentleman and Concurrent Attendant of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, with Fan Zhi and Wang Pu still in office, he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman with concurrent duty in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 時左拾遺、知制誥高錫上封，議武成王廟配享七十二賢，內王僧辯以不令終，恐非全德。

translations.literal: At that time the Left Reminder and Drafter of Edicts Gao Xi submitted a sealed memorial discussing the seventy-two worthies who shared sacrifice in the Temple of King Wucheng, noting that among them Wang Sengbian, because he did not meet a good end, might not possess complete virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder and Edict Drafter Gao Xi then submitted a sealed memorial on the seventy-two worthies who shared sacrifice in the Temple of King Wucheng, arguing that Wang Sengbian—having met a violent end—could scarcely be counted a man of full virtue.

sentences.zh: 尋詔事部尚書張昭、工部尚書竇儀與錫重銓定，功業終始無瑕者方得預焉。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered Minister of the Civil Office Zhang Zhao, Minister of Works Dou Yi, and Xi to reevaluate; only those whose achievements from beginning to end were without flaw were permitted to participate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon ordered Ministers Zhang Zhao and Dou Yi, together with Gao Xi, to reevaluate the roster: only those whose careers from start to finish were without blemish would remain.

sentences.zh: 周翰上言曰：

translations.literal: Zhouhan submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhouhan submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天地以來，覆載之內，聖賢交騖，古今同流，校其顛末，鮮克具美。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that since Heaven and Earth, within what covers and bears all, sages and worthies have raced to and fro; ancient and modern follow the same course; comparing their ends and beginnings, few can fully achieve beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that since Heaven and Earth were formed, sages and worthies have risen in every age under the sky—and when one weighs their beginnings against their ends, scarcely any achieve perfection in full.

sentences.zh: 周公，聖人也，佐武王定天下，輔成王致治平，盛德大勳，蟠天極地。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was a sage; he assisted King Wu to settle the realm and aided King Cheng to attain good governance; his great virtue and great merit coiled through Heaven and reached to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou was a sage: he helped King Wu settle the realm and guided King Cheng to peace; his virtue and achievement filled heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 外則淮夷構難，內則管、蔡流言。

translations.literal: Externally the Huai Yi stirred up trouble; internally Guan and Cai spread slander.
translations.idiomatic: Yet abroad the Huai tribes stirred rebellion, and at home Guan and Cai spread slander against him.

sentences.zh: 疐尾跋胡，垂至顛頓；

translations.literal: The hindquarters tripped and the tail dragged—he nearly came to ruin;
translations.idiomatic: Like a beast whose hind legs falter and tail drags, he nearly came to ruin;

sentences.zh: 偃禾仆木，僅得辨明。

translations.literal: Fallen grain and toppled trees—only then was he able to make things clear.
translations.idiomatic: Only after grain was flattened and trees uprooted did he at last clear his name.

sentences.zh: 此可謂之盡美哉？

translations.literal: Can this be called complete beauty?
translations.idiomatic: Can this be called perfection?

sentences.zh: 臣以為非也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not think so.

sentences.zh: 孔子，聖人也，刪《詩》、《書》，定《禮》、《樂》，祖述堯、舜，憲章文、武。

translations.literal: Confucius was a sage; he edited the Odes and Documents, fixed the Rites and Music, took Yao and Shun as ancestors in the Way, and took Wen and Wu as models in law.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius too was a sage: he edited the Odes and Documents, fixed the Rites and Music, looked back to Yao and Shun, and took King Wen and King Wu as his exemplars.

sentences.zh: 卒以棲遲去魯，奔走厄陳，雖試用於定、哀，曾不容於季、孟。

translations.literal: In the end he lingered in delay and left Lu, ran about and met hardship in Chen; though given trial employment under rulers Ding and Ai, he was never accommodated by Ji and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he lingered in exile from Lu and wandered in distress through Chen; though rulers Ding and Ai gave him trial employment, he never won a secure place under Ji or Meng.

sentences.zh: 又嘗履盜蹠之虎尾，聞南子之珮聲，遠辱慎名，未見其可。

translations.literal: Moreover he once trod on the tiger's tail of the robber Zhi, heard the sound of Nanzi's girdle pendant; from afar these brought disgrace—careful of his reputation, one does not see how these were acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: He once trod perilously close to Robber Zhi and heard the jade of Nanzi at court—acts that even from afar stained his reputation and can hardly be called unimpeachable.

sentences.zh: 此又可謂其盡善者哉？

translations.literal: Can this again be called complete goodness?
translations.idiomatic: Can this be called perfect goodness?

sentences.zh: 臣以為非也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not think so.

sentences.zh: 自餘區區後賢，瑣瑣立事，比於二聖，曾何足雲？

translations.literal: As for the remaining petty later worthies with their trivial achievements, compared with these two sages, how can they be worth speaking of?
translations.idiomatic: As for the lesser worthies who came after, with their small and scattered deeds—what are they beside these two sages?

sentences.zh: 而欲責其磨涅不渝、始卒如一者，臣竊以為難其人矣。

translations.literal: Yet to demand of them that they never change whether polished or stained, being the same from beginning to end—your servant privately considers it would be difficult to find such persons.
translations.idiomatic: To demand that men never change whether polished or stained, remaining wholly consistent from first to last—your servant privately thinks such men are hard to find.

sentences.zh: 昉自唐室，崇祀太公。

translations.literal: Since the Tang dynasty, veneration has been paid in sacrifice to Lord Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang times the court has honored Lord Tai in state sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 原其用意，蓋以天下雖大，不可去兵；

translations.literal: Examining the intent, it was presumably because though the realm is great, arms cannot be dispensed with;
translations.idiomatic: The intent, one may suppose, was that though the realm is vast, arms cannot be done away with;

sentences.zh: 域中有爭，未能無戰。

translations.literal: Within the domain there is strife, and war cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Where the world holds conflict, war cannot altogether be avoided.

sentences.zh: 資其佑民之道，立乎為武之宗，覬張國威，遂進王號。

translations.literal: Relying on his Way of aiding the people, he was established as patriarch of the martial, and aspiring to expand national prestige, he was advanced to princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on his way of protecting the people, the court made him patriarch of the martial arts; hoping to magnify national prestige, it raised him to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 貞元之際，祀典益修，因以歷代武臣陪饗廟貌，如文宣釋奠之制，有弟子列侍之儀，事雖不經，義足垂勸。

translations.literal: At the time of Zhenyuan the sacrificial canon was further refined, and thereby military ministers of successive dynasties were added to share sacrifice in the temple hall, like the Confucian ceremony of the Libation Sacrifice, with the ritual of disciples arrayed in attendance—though the practice was unorthodox, its principle sufficed to hand down encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenyuan reign the rites were further perfected, and martial ministers of successive dynasties were admitted to share sacrifice in the temple, on the model of the Confucian libation ceremony with disciples in attendance. The practice was uncanonical, but its moral purpose was worth preserving.

sentences.zh: 況於曩日，不乏通賢，疑難討論，亦云折中。

translations.literal: Moreover, on former days there was no lack of thoroughly learned worthies; doubtful points were discussed, and it may be said a mean was struck.
translations.idiomatic: In those days learned men were not lacking, and the hard questions were thrashed out until a balanced judgment was reached.

sentences.zh: 今若求其考類，別立否臧，以羔袖之小疵，忘狐裘之大善，恐其所選，僅有可存。

translations.literal: Now if one seeks to examine categories and separately establish approval and disapproval, taking the small flaw of a lamb-sleeve and forgetting the great good of a fox-fur robe, I fear of those selected scarcely any could remain.
translations.idiomatic: If the court now sets out to classify and judge anew—to take a small stain on a lamb's sleeve and forget the great virtue of a fox-fur robe—few of those now honored could survive the culling.

sentences.zh: 隻如樂毅、廉頗，皆奔亡而為虜；

translations.literal: Take for example Yue Yi and Lian Po—all fled in exile and became captives;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yue Yi and Lian Po: both fled into exile and ended as captives;

sentences.zh: 韓信、彭越，悉菹醢而受誅。

translations.literal: Han Xin and Peng Yue—both were minced and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin and Peng Yue were both torn apart and executed.

sentences.zh: 白起則錫劍杜郵，伍員則浮屍江澨。

translations.literal: Bai Qi was granted a sword at Duyou; Wu Yuan's corpse floated on the river shore.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi was ordered to fall on his sword at Duyou; Wu Zixu's body was thrown into the river.

sentences.zh: 左車亦僨軍之將，孫臏實刑餘之人。

translations.literal: Zuo Che was also a general who ruined the army; Sun Bin was truly a man punished by mutilation.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Anling was a general who brought disaster on his army; Sun Bin was a man who had suffered judicial mutilation.

sentences.zh: 穰苴則僨卒齊庭，吳起則非命楚國。

translations.literal: Rangju then ruined the army in the Qi court; Wu Qi met untimely death in the state of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rangju brought the army to ruin in Qi; Wu Qi met a violent end in Chu.

sentences.zh: 周勃稱重，有置甲尚方之疑；

translations.literal: Zhou Bo was held in esteem, yet there was suspicion of keeping armor in the imperial workshop;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bo was a man of weight, yet suspicion clung to him that he had hidden armor in the imperial workshops;

sentences.zh: 陳平善謀，蒙受金諸將之謗。

translations.literal: Chen Ping was skilled in planning, yet bore the slander of receiving gold from various generals.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping was a master strategist, yet was slandered for taking gold from the generals.

sentences.zh: 亞夫則死於獄吏，鄧艾則追於檻車。

translations.literal: Yafu died at the hands of prison clerks; Deng Ai was pursued in the caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yafu died in prison; Deng Ai was hauled away in a prisoner cart.

sentences.zh: 李廣後期而自剄，竇嬰樹黨而喪身。

translations.literal: Li Guang arrived late and cut his own throat; Dou Ying built factional ties and lost his life.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang missed his rendezvous and took his own life; Dou Ying built factional alliances and lost his life for it.

sentences.zh: 鄧禹敗於回溪，終身無董戎之寄；

translations.literal: Deng Yu was defeated at Huixi and throughout his life never received the trust of commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu was routed at Huixi and was never again entrusted with field command.

sentences.zh: 馬援死於蠻徼，還屍闕遣奠之儀。

translations.literal: Ma Yuan died on the barbarian frontier; his returning corpse was denied the ritual of imperial offering.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan died on the barbarian frontier, and his body returning home was denied the court's rites of mourning.

sentences.zh: 其餘諸葛亮之儔，事偏方之主；

translations.literal: Among the rest, those like Zhuge Liang served lords of partial domains;
translations.idiomatic: Then there are men like Zhuge Liang, who served only regional lords;

sentences.zh: 王景略之輩，佐閏位之君。

translations.literal: Those like Wang Jinglue assisted rulers of illegitimate succession.
translations.idiomatic: And men like Wang Jinglue, who aided princes whose titles were irregular.

sentences.zh: 關羽則為仇國所禽，張飛則遭帳下所害。

translations.literal: Guan Yu was captured by the hostile state; Zhang Fei was killed by men under his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu was taken captive by a hostile power, and Zhang Fei was murdered by his own subordinates.

sentences.zh: 凡此名將，悉皆人雄，苟欲指瑕，誰當無累？

translations.literal: All these famous generals were entirely heroes among men; if one wishes to point out flaws, who would be without fault?
translations.idiomatic: Every one of these famous commanders was a hero among men—if one goes looking for flaws, who could claim to be spotless?

sentences.zh: 或從澄汰，盡可棄捐。

translations.literal: If one follows with clarification and elimination, all could be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Apply that standard strictly enough, and every name could be struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 況其功業穹隆，名稱烜赫。

translations.literal: Moreover, their achievements were towering and their reputations brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: Their achievements were towering, their fame resplendent.

sentences.zh: 樵夫牧稚，咸所聞知；

translations.literal: Woodcutters and herd boys all had heard of them;
translations.idiomatic: Woodcutters and herd boys alike had heard of them;

sentences.zh: 列將通侯，竊年思慕。

translations.literal: Ranked generals and enfeoffed lords privately yearned after them in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: ranked generals and enfeoffed lords looked to them in secret admiration.

sentences.zh: 若一旦除去神位，擯出祠庭，吹毛求異代之疵，投袂忿古人之惡，必使時情頓惑，竊議交興。

translations.literal: If at once their spirit tablets were removed and they were banished from the sacrificial hall, picking hairs to seek flaws of another age and shaking one's sleeves in indignation at the wrongs of ancients, it would surely cause present sentiment suddenly to be perplexed and private discussion to rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Strip their spirit tablets from the hall in one stroke, blow on a speck of dust to find fault with men of another age, flare up in indignation at ancient wrongs—and you will surely bewilder the living and set loose a storm of private murmuring.

sentences.zh: 景行高山，更奚瞻於往躅；

translations.literal: The lofty conduct of the high mountain—what further need to look upon past footsteps;
translations.idiomatic: The high exemplar stands like a mountain—why must anyone still measure old footsteps;

sentences.zh: 英魂烈魄，將有恨於明時。

translations.literal: Their heroic souls and fierce spirits would harbor resentment toward this enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: their heroic spirits would carry grievance into this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 況伏陛下方厲軍威，將遏亂略，講求兵法，締構武祠，蓋所以勸激戎臣，資假陰助。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty is now vigorously promoting military prestige, about to curb disorder and upheaval, studying military methods, and building martial temples—this is all to encourage and rouse military officials and lend them hidden aid.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty is now strengthening the army's prestige, checking disorder, studying the arts of war, and founding martial shrines—all to stir military men to valor and lend them unseen support.

sentences.zh: 忽使長廊虛邈，僅有可圖之形；

translations.literal: Suddenly to make the long corridor empty and distant, with barely any figures left to depict;
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the long corridor would stand empty, scarcely a figure left upon the walls;

sentences.zh: 中殿前空，不見配食之坐。

translations.literal: The front hall empty, with no seats for shared sacrifice visible.
translations.idiomatic: the central hall bare, with no companion worthies seated for shared sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 似非允當，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: This seems not appropriate; your servant is privately troubled.
translations.idiomatic: That hardly seems fitting—and your servant is deeply troubled by it.

sentences.zh: 深惟事貴得中，用資體要，若今之可以議古，恐來者亦能非今。

translations.literal: Deeply considering that affairs are valued for hitting the mean and for embodying essentials, if what is done today can be used to judge antiquity, I fear those who come after will also be able to condemn the present.
translations.idiomatic: Matters are best judged by the mean and the essential: if today's standard is applied to judge the past, those who come after may just as well condemn the present.

sentences.zh: 願納臣微忠，特追明敕，乞下此疏，廷議其長。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will accept your servant's humble loyalty, specially issue a clear edict, and order this memorial transmitted so the court may debate its merits.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed this humble counsel, issue a clarifying edict, and submit this memorial for open debate at court.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，獻《擬製》二十編，擢為右拾遺。

translations.literal: During Qiande, he submitted twenty fascicles of "Imperial Drafts" and was promoted to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande period he submitted twenty fascicles of "Imperial Drafts" and was promoted to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 會修大內，上《五鳳樓賦》，人多傳誦之。

translations.literal: When the inner palace was being renovated, he submitted the "Ode to the Five Phoenix Tower," and many people passed it along and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: During renovations of the inner palace he submitted an "Ode to the Five Phoenix Tower," which many copied and recited.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，文體卑弱，周翰與高錫、柳開、範杲習尚淳古，齊名友善，當時有「高、梁、柳、範」之稱。

translations.literal: Since the Five Dynasties, literary style had been base and weak; Zhouhan together with Gao Xi, Liu Kai, and Fan Gao practiced the ancient pure style, were equally famous and friendly, and at the time were called the "Gao, Liang, Liu, and Fan" group.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties literary taste had sunk low; Zhouhan, together with Gao Xi, Liu Kai, and Fan Gao, revived the plain antique style, were famous friends, and were known as the "Four—Gao, Liang, Liu, and Fan."

sentences.zh: 初，太祖嘗識彥溫於軍中，石守信亦與彥溫舊故。

translations.literal: Earlier, Taizu had once recognized Yanwen in the army, and Shi Shouxin was also an old acquaintance of Yanwen's.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu had known Yanwen in the army, and Shi Shouxin was also an old friend of his.

sentences.zh: 一日，太祖語守信，將用周翰掌誥，守信微露其言，周翰遽上表謝。

translations.literal: One day the Taizu Emperor spoke to Shouxin, saying he intended to appoint Zhouhan to manage imperial edicts; Shouxin slightly revealed this in speech, and Zhouhan hastily submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: One day Taizu told Shouxin he meant to put Zhouhan in charge of imperial edicts; Shouxin let the hint slip, and Zhouhan at once submitted a note of thanks.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，遂寢其命。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and therefore shelved the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and dropped the appointment.

sentences.zh: 曆通判綿、眉二州，在眉州坐杖人至死，奪二官。

translations.literal: He served successively as judicial commissioner of Mian and Mei Prefectures; while in Meizhou he was demoted two ranks for beating a man to death with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as judicial commissioner of Mian and Mei; in Mei he beat a man to death with the rod and was stripped of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 起授太子左讚善大夫。

translations.literal: He was restored and appointed Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was reinstated as Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，遷右拾遺，監綾綿院，改左補闕兼知大理正事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he was transferred to Right Reminder, overseer of the Brocade and Silk Bureau, and changed to Left Supplementation Censor concurrently managing chief judge affairs of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 970 he became Right Reminder and overseer of the brocade depot, then Left Supplementation Censor with charge of chief judge duties at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 會將郊祀，因上疏曰：「陛下再郊上帝，必覃赦宥。

translations.literal: When a suburban sacrifice to Heaven was impending, he therefore submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty, having twice performed suburban sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, will surely grant a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: As a suburban sacrifice drew near he memorialized: "Your Majesty has twice sacrificed to Heaven at the suburban altar and will surely proclaim a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 臣以天下至大，其中有慶澤所未及、節文所未該者，所宜推而廣之。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that within the realm, which is greatest, there are matters where gracious favor has not yet reached and where ritual provisions have not yet covered—all of which should be extended and broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in so vast a realm there remain corners where the gracious edict has not reached and categories its ritual language does not cover—areas that ought to be extended and enlarged.

sentences.zh: 方今賦稅年入至多，加以科變之物，名品非一，調發供輸，不無重困。

translations.literal: At present annual tax revenues are exceedingly great, and additional items under separate exaction lists are not of one kind; mobilization for delivery and transport is not without heavy hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Tax receipts have grown enormous, and the additional items exacted under separate lists are legion; levies and transport still crush the people.

sentences.zh: 且西蜀、淮南、荊、潭、廣、桂之地，皆以為王土。

translations.literal: Moreover the lands of Western Shu, Huainan, Jing, Tan, Guang, and Gui are all regarded as royal territory.
translations.idiomatic: Western Shu, Huainan, Jing, Tan, Guang, and Gui are now all imperial soil.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能以三方所得之利，減諸道租賦之入，則庶乎均德澤而寬民力矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can indeed use the profit obtained from those three regions to reduce the tax revenues levied in the various circuits, then it would be roughly equal in virtuous favor and would ease the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty were to apply the revenue of those conquered regions to lighten the tax burdens of the other circuits, favor would be spread more evenly and the people's load eased.

sentences.zh: 」俄坐杖錦工過差，為其所訴。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he was impeached because he exceeded proper measure in beating a brocade artisan.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after he was denounced for excessive beating of a brocade artisan.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚怒，責之曰：「爾豈不知人之膚血與己無異，何乃遽為酷罰！

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor was very angry and rebuked him, saying: "Do you not know that other men's flesh and blood are no different from your own—why then so hastily inflict cruel punishment!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was furious: "Do you not know another man's flesh and blood is the same as your own? Why deal out cruel punishment so quickly!

sentences.zh: 」將杖之，周翰自言：「臣負天下才名，不當如是。

translations.literal: " He was about to beat Zhouhan with the rod, and Zhouhan said of himself: "Your servant bears a great name in the realm and ought not to be treated thus.
translations.idiomatic: " As the rod was raised Zhouhan said: "I am a man of wide renown in the empire—I should not be treated like this.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃解，止左授司農寺丞。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon relented and only demoted him to left assignment as Vice Director of the Directorate of Grains.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu relented and demoted him only to Vice Director of the Directorate of Grains.

sentences.zh: 逾年，為太子中允。

translations.literal: After a year he was made Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，知蘇州。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he governed Suzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo period he served as prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 周翰善音律，喜蒱博，惟以飲戲為務。

translations.literal: Zhouhan was skilled at music and fond of betting games; he devoted himself solely to drinking and play.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouhan loved music and gambling and gave himself over chiefly to drink and games.

sentences.zh: 州有伶官錢氏，家數百人，日令百人供妓，每出，必以殽具自隨。

translations.literal: In the prefecture there was an entertainer of the Qian clan whose household numbered several hundred persons; each day she had a hundred persons supply courtesans, and whenever she went out she always had dishes and utensils follow her.
translations.idiomatic: A troupe leader of the Qian clan kept a household of hundreds and every day maintained a hundred entertainers; whenever she went abroad a train of food and wine followed.

sentences.zh: 郡務不治，以本官分司西京。

translations.literal: Prefectural affairs went untended, and on account of his original office he was assigned to a post in the Western Capital as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural business was neglected, and he was relegated to an honorary posting at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 逾月，授左讚善大夫，仍分司。

translations.literal: After a month he was appointed Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent, still serving as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was made Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent, still in honorary service.

sentences.zh: 俄除楚州團練副使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Chuzhou Militia.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Chuzhou militia.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，宰相李昉以其名聞，召為右補闕，賜緋魚，使江、淮提點茶鹽。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, Chancellor Li Fang because of his fame summoned him as Right Supplementation Censor, granted him the red robe and fish tally, and sent him to inspect tea and salt in the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi Chancellor Li Fang, on his reputation, recalled him as Right Supplementation Censor, granted the red robe and fish tally, and dispatched him to inspect tea and salt in the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 周翰以辭學為流輩所許，頻曆外任，不樂吏事。

translations.literal: Zhouhan, because his literary learning was approved by his generation, frequently held outer posts and did not delight in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His peers acknowledged his literary talent, but he served repeatedly in the provinces and took little pleasure in administration.

sentences.zh: 會翰林學士宋白等列奏其有史才，回下位，遂命兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: When Hanlin Academician Song Bai and others jointly memorialized that he had historiographical talent, he was returned to a lower capital post and thereupon ordered concurrently to compile in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Bai and other Hanlin academicians testified to his gifts as a historian, he was brought back to the capital and named a concurrent compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 會太宗親試貢士，周翰為考官，麵賜金紫，因語宰相，稱其有文，尋遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: When the Taizong Emperor personally tested examination candidates, Zhouhan was an examiner; face to face he was bestowed gold and purple, and speaking to the chancellors he praised Zhouhan's literary gifts; soon he was transferred to Diarist of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong personally examined candidates, Zhouhan served as examiner, was granted gold and purple in audience, and so impressed the chancellor that he was soon made Diarist of Attendance.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，張佖建議復置左右史之職，乃命周翰與李宗諤分領之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, Zhang Bie proposed restoring the posts of Left and Right Scribe; Zhouhan and Li Zong'e were ordered to divide leadership of them.
translations.idiomatic: In 994 Zhang Bie proposed reviving the Left and Right Scribes; Zhouhan and Li Zong'e were placed in charge.

sentences.zh: 周翰兼起居郎，因上言：「自今崇政、長春殿皇帝宣諭之言，侍臣諭列之事，望依舊中書修為時政記。

translations.literal: Zhouhan concurrently served as Attendance Diarist and therefore submitted a memorial saying: "From now on, words the emperor proclaims in the Chongzheng and Changchun halls and matters attendant ministers explain to the court—I hope that, following the old practice, the Secretariat will compile them into a Record of Current Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouhan, also Attendance Diarist, memorialized: "Henceforth the emperor's pronouncements in the Chongzheng and Changchun halls and the attendant ministers' business before the court should, as of old, be compiled by the Secretariat into a Record of Current Administration.

sentences.zh: 其樞密院事涉機密，亦令本院編纂，每至月終送史館。

translations.literal: Matters of the Bureau of Military Affairs that touch on secrets should also be compiled by that bureau itself and sent to the Historiography Institute at each month's end.
translations.idiomatic: Secret matters of the Bureau of Military Affairs should be compiled by that bureau and sent monthly to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 自餘百司凡於對拜、除改、沿革、製置之事，悉條報本院，以備編錄。

translations.literal: Among the remaining hundred offices, all matters of audience, appointments and dismissals, institutional changes, and regulatory establishments should be itemized and reported to this office to prepare for compilation and record.
translations.idiomatic: All other agencies should report audiences, appointments, institutional changes, and new regulations to this office for the record.

sentences.zh: 仍令郎與舍人分直崇政殿，以記言動，別為起居注，每月先進禦，後降付史館。

translations.literal: Moreover let the Attendance Diarist and Diarist of Attendance divide duty at the Chongzheng Hall to record words and actions, separately keeping a Record of Attendance; each month it should first be submitted to the emperor, then sent down to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Let Attendance Diarist and Diarist of Attendance share watch at Chongzheng Hall, keep a separate Record of Attendance, submit it to the emperor each month first, then pass it to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved.

sentences.zh: 起居注進禦，自周翰等始也。

translations.literal: The Record of Attendance submitted to the emperor began with Zhouhan and his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly presentation of the Record of Attendance to the throne began with Zhouhan and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 周翰蚤有時譽，久擯廢，及被除擢，尤洽時論。

translations.literal: Zhouhan early enjoyed contemporary repute; long cast aside, when he received appointment and promotion public opinion was especially satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Long famous and long sidelined, he at last won appointment—and public opinion warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 會考課京朝官，有敢隱前犯者，皆除名為民。

translations.literal: When capital officials of the Examination Bureau were evaluated, those who dared conceal previous offenses were all stripped of office and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: During the review of capital officials, anyone who concealed prior offenses was cashiered and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 周翰被譴尤多，所上有司偶遺一事，當免。

translations.literal: The censures against Zhouhan were especially numerous; in what he submitted to the proper offices one matter happened to be omitted and he should have been exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The censures against Zhouhan were especially numerous; one offense was accidentally omitted from his submission and he might have escaped dismissal.

sentences.zh: 判館楊徽之率三館學士詣相府，以為周翰非故有規避，其實所犯頻繁，不能悉記，於是止罰金百斤。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Institute Yang Huizhi led the Three Repositories academicians to the chancellor's office, arguing that Zhouhan had not deliberately evaded on purpose but that in truth his offenses were frequent and could not all be remembered; therefore he was only fined a hundred catties of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huizhi, supervisor of the institute, led the Three Repositories academicians to the chancellery to argue that Zhouhan had not willfully concealed his record but had simply committed too many lapses to remember—whereupon he was fined only a hundred catties of copper.

sentences.zh: 先是，趙安易建議於西川鑄大鐵錢，以一當十，周翰上言：「古者貨、幣、錢三者兼用，若錢少於貨、幣，即鑄大錢，或當百，或當五十，蓋欲廣其錢而足用爾。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhao Anrong had proposed casting large iron coins in Western Shu, one counted as ten; Zhouhan submitted a memorial saying: "In antiquity goods, silk tokens, and coin were used together; if coin was fewer than goods and silk tokens, large coin was cast, sometimes counting as a hundred, sometimes as fifty—the intent was simply to expand coinage and make it sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhao Anrong had proposed minting large iron coins in Sichuan at ten to one; Zhouhan argued: "Antiquity used goods, silk tokens, and coin together; when coin ran short, large denominations were cast—sometimes worth fifty or a hundred—to stretch the supply.

sentences.zh: 今不若使蜀民貿易者，凡鐵錢一止作一錢用，官中市物即以兩錢當一。

translations.literal: Now it would be better to have the people of Shu engaged in trade use each iron coin as one coin only, while in government market purchases two coins would count as one.
translations.idiomatic: Better that Sichuan traders treat each iron piece as one coin in private exchange, while the government accept two for one in official markets.

sentences.zh: 又西川患在少鹽，請於益州置榷院，入物交易，則公私通濟矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Western Shu suffers from scarcity of salt; I request establishing a monopoly bureau at Yizhou where goods are brought in and exchanged—then public and private interests will all be accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan also lacks salt; establish a monopoly exchange at Yizhou where goods can be traded in, and both public treasury and people will be served.

sentences.zh: 」至道中，遷工部郎中。

translations.literal: " In the Zhidao period he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Zhidao period he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 周翰性疏雋卞急，臨事過於嚴暴，故多曠敗。

translations.literal: Zhouhan by nature was unrestrained, sharp, and abrupt; in handling affairs he was excessively stern and violent, and therefore often failed through neglect.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was sharp, restless, and headstrong; in office he was harsh to excess and often failed through neglect.

sentences.zh: 晚年才思稍減，書詔多不稱旨。

translations.literal: In his later years his literary talent slightly declined, and many edicts he drafted did not satisfy intent.
translations.idiomatic: In later years his literary powers waned, and many edicts he drafted missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 有集五十卷及《續因話錄》。

translations.literal: He had a collection of fifty scrolls and a "Continued Record of Casual Conversations."
translations.idiomatic: He left a fifty-scroll collection and a "Continued Record of Casual Conversations."

sentences.zh: 朱昂，字舉之，其先京兆人，世家渼陂。

translations.literal: Zhu Ang, styled Juzhi, his ancestors were from Jingzhao, a family long established at Meibei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ang, courtesy name Juzhi, came of a Jingzhao family long settled at Meibei.

sentences.zh: 唐天復末，徙家南陽。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang Tianfu, the family moved to Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tang Tianfu era the family moved to Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 梁祖篡唐，父葆光與唐舊臣顏蕘、李濤數輩挈家南渡，寓潭州。

translations.literal: When Liang's founder usurped Tang, his father Baoguang together with several old Tang ministers including Yan Rao and Li Tao took their families south and sojourned in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder usurped the Tang, his father Baoguang joined several old Tang ministers, including Yan Rao and Li Tao, in taking their families south to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 每正旦夕至，必序立南嶽祠前，北望號慟，殆二十年。

translations.literal: Every dawn and dusk they would line up in order before the Southern Peak temple, look north and wail— for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: At every dawn and dusk they would stand in order before the Southern Peak temple, look north, and wail—for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 後濤北歸，葆光樂衡山之勝，遂往家焉。

translations.literal: Later Tao returned north; Baoguang delighted in the beauty of Mount Heng and went to make his home there.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Tao returned north; Baoguang, enchanted by Mount Heng, made his home there.

sentences.zh: 昂少與熊若穀、鄧洵美同學。

translations.literal: Ang in youth studied with Xiong Rugu and Deng Xunmei.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ang studied with Xiong Rugu and Deng Xunmei.

sentences.zh: 朱遵度好讀書，人號之為「朱萬卷」，目昂為「小萬卷」。

translations.literal: Zhu Zundu loved reading books and people called him "Zhu of Ten Thousand Scrolls"; they called Ang "Little Ten Thousand Scrolls."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zundu loved books and was called "Zhu of Ten Thousand Scrolls"; Ang they nicknamed "Little Ten Thousand Scrolls."

sentences.zh: 昂嘗間行經廬陵，道遇異人，謂之曰：「中原不久當有真主平一天下，子仕至四品，安用南為？

translations.literal: Ang once traveled by side paths through Luling and met an extraordinary man who said to him: "Before long the Central Plains will have a true lord who pacifies all under Heaven; you will reach the fourth rank—of what use is the south?
translations.idiomatic: Ang once traveled by side paths through Luling and met a stranger who told him: "Before long the Central Plains will have a true lord who unifies the realm; you will rise to the fourth rank—why linger in the south?

sentences.zh: 」遂北遊江、淮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he traveled north to the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: " He went north to the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 時周世宗南征，韓令坤統兵至揚州，昂謁見，陳治亂方略，令坤奇之，署權知揚州揚子縣。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong of Later Zhou was on southern campaign; Han Lingkun commanded troops to Yangzhou; Ang had audience, set forth strategy for order and chaos; Lingkun was struck by it and appointed him acting magistrate of Yangzi County in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Zhou's Shizong marched south, Han Lingkun led troops to Yangzhou; Ang presented him with a strategy for order and chaos, impressed him, and was appointed acting magistrate of Yangzi County.

sentences.zh: 適兵革之際，逃亡過半，昂便宜綏輯，復逋亡者七千餘家，令坤即表授本縣令。

translations.literal: Right in the midst of warfare, over half had fled; Ang appropriately soothed and settled them and recovered more than seven thousand fleeing households; Lingkun immediately memorialized and granted him the full magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: War had emptied half the county; Ang eased conditions as he could, brought back more than seven thousand refugee households, and Lingkun at once memorialized to confirm him as full magistrate.

sentences.zh: 宋初，為衡州錄事參軍，嘗讀陶潛《閑情賦》而慕之，因廣其辭曰：

translations.literal: Early in Song he was Recorder of Heng Prefecture; he once read Tao Qian's "Rhapsody on Leisurely Sentiment" and admired it, and therefore expanded its phrases, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he served as recorder of Heng Prefecture; reading Tao Qian's "Rhapsody on Leisurely Sentiment," he admired it and expanded its language, writing:

sentences.zh: 維稟氣兮清濁，獨得意兮虛徐。

translations.literal: Only in clear and turbid endowment, alone at ease with emptiness and leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving breath of clear or turbid, alone I rest easy and unhurried.

sentences.zh: 耳何聰兮無瑱，衣何散兮無裾。

translations.literal: Why should ears be keen yet pierced, why should garments hang loose without hems?
translations.idiomatic: Ears need no piercing to hear; robes need no hems to drape.

sentences.zh: 務冥懷於得喪，寧勤體乎菑畬。

translations.literal: I seek to hold in dark bosom gain and loss, rather than wear out the body in field and furrow.
translations.idiomatic: Better to harbor gain and loss in silence than wear the body thin at plow and hoe.

sentences.zh: 將使同方姬、孔，抗跡孫、蘧。

translations.literal: I would make men share the way of Ji and Kong, and stride as equals with Sun and Qu.
translations.idiomatic: I would stand with Ji and Confucius in the Way, and match stride with Sun and Qu.

sentences.zh: 精騖廣漠，心遊太虛。

translations.literal: Spirit races the wide desert, heart roams the Great Void.
translations.idiomatic: My spirit races the wild wastes; my heart wanders the Great Void.

sentences.zh: 傲朝曦兮南榮，溯夕飆兮北疏。

translations.literal: I scorn the morning sun on the southern eaves, and meet the evening wind at the northern window.
translations.idiomatic: I greet no morning sun on the southern beam, nor chase the evening gust at the northern casement.

sentences.zh: 非道之病，惟情之舒。

translations.literal: This is not the Way's sickness—only feeling set free.
translations.idiomatic: Not sickness of the Way, but feeling let loose.

sentences.zh: 繇是含穎懷粹，凝和習懿。

translations.literal: Hence holding the bud, nurturing the pure, gathering harmony and practicing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: So I sheathe the bud within, gather purity, collect harmony, and cultivate goodness.

sentences.zh: 器奫淪兮幽憂，德芬馨兮周比。

translations.literal: Vessel deep and submerged in quiet sorrow, virtue fragrant and mingling with those around.
translations.idiomatic: The vessel sinks deep in quiet grief; virtue spreads fragrance among my kin.

sentences.zh: 井無渫兮泉融，珠潛輝兮川媚。

translations.literal: A well untroubled, its spring merges; a pearl hidden, its river shines.
translations.idiomatic: Untroubled wells merge their springs; pearls hidden still make the river glow.

sentences.zh: 又何必陋雄之尚《玄》，笑奕之心醉，悲墨之素絲，歎展之下位？

translations.literal: Why then scorn Yang Xiong's esteem for the Dark Classic, laugh at Yi's drunken heart, mourn Mo Zi's white silk, or sigh at Zhan's low station?
translations.idiomatic: Why scorn Yang Xiong's worship of the Dark Classic, laugh at the chess player's drunken heart, grieve over Mo Di's white silk, or lament Zhan's lowly place?

sentences.zh: 苟因時之明揚，乃斯文之不墜。

translations.literal: If once there is enlightened elevation according to the times, then this culture will not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the age lifts the worthy in due season, culture itself will not fall.

sentences.zh: 睇煙景兮飄飄，心懸旌兮搖搖。

translations.literal: Gazing at misty vistas, they drift and billow; my heart's banners flutter and sway.
translations.idiomatic: I watch the misted landscape billow; banners of the heart flutter and sway.

sentences.zh: 感朝榮而夕落，嗟響蛩而鳴蜩。

translations.literal: Morning glory withers by evening—a sigh at crickets and chirping cicadas.
translations.idiomatic: Morning bloom fades by night—so I sigh with the cricket and the summer cicada.

sentences.zh: 姑藏器以有待，因寄物而長謠。

translations.literal: For a time I hide my vessel and wait; I send a long song through what lies near.
translations.idiomatic: For now I hide my talent and wait, and pour a long song through what lies near at hand.

sentences.zh: 願在首而為弁，束玄發而未衰。

translations.literal: I would be the cap on the head, binding dark hair still undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were the cap upon the head, binding black locks still unthinned.

sentences.zh: 會名器之有得，與纓珥兮相宜。

translations.literal: When name and vessel are gained, cap-tassels and ear-pendants suit one well.
translations.idiomatic: When name and office are won, cap-tassels and ear-pendants sit fit upon me.

sentences.zh: 願在足而為舄，何坎險之罹憂。

translations.literal: I would be shoes on the feet—why then suffer care at pits and peril?
translations.idiomatic: Would I were shoes upon the feet—why suffer the pits and perils of the path?

sentences.zh: 欲效勤於豎亥，思追踵於浮丘。

translations.literal: I would toil like the slave Shuahai, and think to follow in the footsteps of Fu Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: I would serve like Shuahai in toil, and follow in the steps of Fu Qiu.

sentences.zh: 願在服而為袂，傳繒素而飾躬。

translations.literal: I would be the sleeve upon the robe, passing silk and fine gauze to adorn the body.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were the sleeve on the robe, spreading silk and fine gauze to dress the body.

sentences.zh: 異化緇之色涅，寧拭麵而道窮。

translations.literal: Unlike black cloth that changes in the dye, I would rather wipe the face though the Way comes to an end.
translations.idiomatic: Unlike cloth that blackens in dye, I would wipe the face even when the Way runs out.

sentences.zh: 願在目而為鑒，分妍醜於崇朝。

translations.literal: I would be the mirror before the eyes, sorting beauty from ugliness in the bright morning.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were the mirror before the eyes, sorting fair from foul at the break of day.

sentences.zh: 驚青陽之難久，庶白首以見招。

translations.literal: Startled that the green spring cannot last, I hope at white-haired age to be summoned still.
translations.idiomatic: I dread that green spring cannot endure—yet hope white age may yet be called.

sentences.zh: 願在地而為簟，當暑溽而冰寒。

translations.literal: I would be the mat upon the ground, in sweltering heat offering chill as ice.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were the sleeping mat on the ground, turning summer heat to ice-cold ease.

sentences.zh: 伊膚革之尚疚，胡寤寐以求安？

translations.literal: Since skin and hide still bear sore distress, how in sleep and waking can one seek rest?
translations.idiomatic: Yet skin and hide still smart with hurt—how then seek rest waking or asleep?

sentences.zh: 願在觴而為醴，不亂德而溺真。

translations.literal: Would I be the sweet wine in the cup, not confounding virtue and drowning the true self.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were the wine in the cup, never muddling virtue or drowning what is true.

sentences.zh: 體虛受之為器，革譎性以歸淳。

translations.literal: Emptied within to receive as a vessel, changing a cunning nature to return to purity.
translations.idiomatic: Hollow within to hold what comes, I would shed cunning and return to what is plain.

sentences.zh: 願在握而為劍，每輔衽而保裾。

translations.literal: Would I be a sword in the grip, always aiding the robe's border and guarding the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were the sword in the hand, ever steadying the robe and guarding the hem.

sentences.zh: 殊鉛銛之效用，比硎刃而有餘。

translations.literal: Surpassing the utility of lead and sharpness, compared to a whetstone's edge having surplus.
translations.idiomatic: More useful than lead or mere sharpness—like an edge honed on stone, and still to spare.

sentences.zh: 願在橐而為矢，美筈羽之斯全。

translations.literal: Would I be an arrow in the quiver, perfect in its nock and fletching.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were the arrow in the quiver, whole in shaft and feather.

sentences.zh: 疇懋勳而錫晉，射窮壘而衄燕。

translations.literal: Once for great merit granted Jin, shooting exhausted fortresses and repulsing Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Once for merit enfeoffed in Jin, shooting till the ramparts fell and driving Yan back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 願在體而為裘，托針縷以成功。

translations.literal: Would I be fur on the body, relying on needle and thread to achieve completion.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were the fur upon the body, stitched into being by needle and thread.

sentences.zh: 非珍華而取飾，將被服而有容。

translations.literal: Not taking adornment from rare splendor, but to be worn and have bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Not for rare display, but to be worn and lend dignity.

sentences.zh: 願在軒而為篁，貫歲寒而不改。

translations.literal: Would I be bamboo in the hall, passing through cold years unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Would I were bamboo in the hall, enduring the cold years unaltered.

sentences.zh: 挺介節以自持，廓虛心而有待。

translations.literal: Upright in integrity to hold oneself, opening an empty heart to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Upright in integrity, empty in heart, and waiting still.

sentences.zh: 人之願兮實繁，我之心兮若此。

translations.literal: Men's wishes are indeed manifold; my heart is as this.
translations.idiomatic: The wishes of men are many; my heart is only this.

sentences.zh: 蓄為誌兮璞藏，發為文兮霧委。

translations.literal: Stored as aspiration, a jade hid; released as writing, like mist spreading.
translations.idiomatic: Aspiration stored like jade hidden; writing released like mist unrolling.

sentences.zh: 既持瑾兮掌瑜，復擷蘭兮藝芷。

translations.literal: Already holding jade in the palm, again gathering orchids and cultivating angelica.
translations.idiomatic: Jade in the hand, orchids gathered, angelica cultivated.

sentences.zh: 始無言兮植杖，終俯首兮嗟髀。

translations.literal: At first wordless, planting the staff; at last bowing the head, sighing at the thighs.
translations.idiomatic: First wordless with staff planted; at last bowing the head and sighing over wasted legs.

sentences.zh: 振襟兮自適，覿物兮解頤。

translations.literal: Shaking out the robes in self-content, meeting things and loosening the chin.
translations.idiomatic: I shake out my robe and rest easy; I meet the world and smile.

sentences.zh: 雲無心兮遐舉，蘿倚幹兮叢滋。

translations.literal: Cloud without heart rises afar; creepers lean on the trunk in clustered growth.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds rise without intent; creepers lean on the trunk and multiply.

sentences.zh: 想陵谷之變地，況玄黃之易絲。

translations.literal: Thinking of hills and valleys changing place, let alone black and yellow swapping silk.
translations.idiomatic: If hills and valleys can shift, how much more may black and yellow change their hue.

sentences.zh: 人可汰而可鍛，己不磷而不緇。

translations.literal: Others may be washed and forged; oneself neither tarnished nor blackened.
translations.idiomatic: Others may be washed and tempered; I would neither stain nor blacken.

sentences.zh: 苟一鳴而驚人，何五鼎而勿飴？

translations.literal: If once a call startles men, why would five tripods not be sweet?
translations.idiomatic: If one cry can startle the world, why refuse the sweetness of the five tripods?

sentences.zh: 已而擁膝清嘯，傾懷自寬。

translations.literal: Then hugging the knees in clear whistling, pouring out the bosom to ease oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Then hugging my knees I whistle clear and pour out my heart to ease myself.

sentences.zh: 樞桑戶蓽兮差樂，鳩飛梭躍兮胡難。

translations.literal: Mulberry door and thatched gate—perhaps some joy; dove flying and shuttle leaping—how difficult.
translations.idiomatic: A mulberry door and thatched gate may suffice for joy; but dove in flight and shuttle in leap—how hard they are.

sentences.zh: 指夜蟾兮為伍，仰疏籟兮邀歡。

translations.literal: Pointing to the night moon as companion, looking up at sparse rustlings to invite delight.
translations.idiomatic: I take the night moon as my companion and lift my ear to the sparse wind for delight.

sentences.zh: 何孫牧而伊耕？

translations.literal: Why Sun Shu herding and Yi Yin plowing?
translations.idiomatic: Why Sun Shu with his cattle, Yi Yin at the plow?

sentences.zh: 何巢箕而呂磻？

translations.literal: Why Chao Fu washing at the stream and Lü Wang fishing?
translations.idiomatic: Why Chao washing by the stream, Lü Wang with his line?

sentences.zh: 滌我慮兮綠綺。

translations.literal: Washing my cares on the green lute.
translations.idiomatic: I wash my cares upon the green lute.

sentences.zh: 清我眠兮琅玕。

translations.literal: Clearing my sleep on jade bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: I clear my sleep upon jade bamboo.

sentences.zh: 周旋兮有則，徙倚兮可觀。

translations.literal: In turning about there is rule; lingering and leaning is worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: In coming and going there is measure; in lingering there is something worth seeing.

sentences.zh: 終卷舒兮自得，契休哉於《考槃》。

translations.literal: At last rolling and unrolling in self-content, matching the joy of "Kaopan."
translations.idiomatic: At last I roll and unroll content, and find my joy in the "Kaopan."

sentences.zh: 李昉知州事，暇日多召語，且以文為贄，昉深所嗟賞。

translations.literal: Li Fang, governing the prefecture, in his leisure often summoned Ang to converse and accepted his writings as tribute; Fang deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang, as prefect, often called him to talk in his spare time and accepted his writings as gifts; Fang admired him deeply.

sentences.zh: 曆宜城令。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，拜太子洗馬、知蓬州，徙廣安軍。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and governor of Pengzhou, then transferred to Guang'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao he became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and governor of Pengzhou, then was moved to Guang'an Army.

sentences.zh: 會渠州妖賊李仙眾萬人劫掠軍界，昂設策禽之。

translations.literal: When the bandit Li Xian of Quzhou with ten thousand men plundered the military border, Ang devised a strategy and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Quzhou bandit Li Xian led ten thousand men in raiding the military frontier, Ang devised a plan and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 自餘果、合、渝、涪四州民連結為妖者，置不問，蜀民遂安。

translations.literal: As for the remaining people of Guo, He, Yu, and Fu who had banded together in sorcery, he left them unpursued, and the people of Shu thus found peace.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest who in Guo, He, Yu, and Fu had joined in sorcery, he chose not to pursue them, and the people of Shu were settled.

sentences.zh: 宰相薛居正稱其能，遷殿中丞、知泗州。

translations.literal: Chancellor Xue Juzheng praised his ability, and he was transferred to Palace Aide and governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xue Juzheng commended his competence, and he was promoted to Palace Aide and made prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗作《隋河辭》，謂浚決之病民，遊觀之傷財，乃天意之所以亡隋也。

translations.literal: He once wrote the "Rhapsody on the Sui River," saying that dredging harmed the people and touring wasted wealth—these were how Heaven's intent destroyed Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed a "Rhapsody on the Sui River," arguing that dredging oppressed the people and pleasure tours wasted the treasury—Heaven's way of destroying Sui.

sentences.zh: 使隋不興役費財以害其民，則安得有今日之利哉！

translations.literal: Had Sui not raised corvée and spent wealth to harm its people, how could there be today's profit!
translations.idiomatic: Had Sui not spent its people and wealth on forced labor, how would the present realm enjoy today's gain?

sentences.zh: 嘗聚淮水流屍三千，為塚瘞之。

translations.literal: Once he gathered three thousand corpses from the Huai River and buried them in a mound.
translations.idiomatic: He once collected three thousand corpses from the Huai River and buried them in a common mound.

sentences.zh: 有戍卒謀亂，昂誅其首惡，凡支黨之詿誤者悉貰之。

translations.literal: When garrison soldiers plotted rebellion, Ang executed the ringleaders and pardoned all followers implicated in error.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison troops plotted revolt, Ang put the ringleaders to death and pardoned all who had been drawn in by mistake.

sentences.zh: 就遷監察御史、江南轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was immediately transferred to Investigating Censor and Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once made Investigating Censor and Vice Transport Commissioner for Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，知鄂州，加殿中侍御史，為峽路轉運副使，就改庫部員外郎，遷轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he governed Ezhou, was promoted to Attendant Palace Aide, served as Vice Transport Commissioner of the Gorges route, was concurrently made Deputy Director of the Ministry of Stores, and then Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 977 he governed Ezhou, became Attendant Palace Aide, Vice Transport Commissioner for the Gorges route, Deputy Director of the Ministry of Stores, and finally Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，以本官直秘閣，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, with his original office he served concurrently in the Secret Archive and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: In 989, retaining his rank, he entered the Secret Archive and received the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 久之，出知復州，表求謝事，不許。

translations.literal: After a long time he was sent out as governor of Fuzhou; he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was posted prefect of Fuzhou; he asked to retire, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 遷水部郎中，復請老，召還，再直秘閣，尋兼越王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Waterways, again requested retirement on grounds of age, was recalled, again served in the Secret Archive, and soon also became Recorder of the Prince of Yue's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Director of the Ministry of Waterways, he again pleaded age to retire, was recalled, re-entered the Secret Archive, and soon became Recorder in the Prince of Yue's household.

sentences.zh: 直宗即位，遷秩司封郎中，俄知制誥，判史館，受詔編次三館秘閣書籍，既畢，加吏部。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Ang's rank was raised to Director of the Department of Enfeoffments; soon he became Edict Drafter and supervised the Historiography Institute; ordered to compile the books of the Three Repositories and Secret Archive—when finished, he was promoted to the Ministry of the Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Ang rose to Director of the Department of Enfeoffments, then Edict Drafter with charge of the Historiography Institute; ordered to catalogue the Three Repositories and Secret Archive, he was promoted to the Ministry of the Civil Office when the work was done.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as Academic Laureate.
translations.idiomatic: In 999 he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academic laureate.

sentences.zh: 逾年，拜章乞骸骨，召對，敦諭，請彌確，乃拜工部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: After a year he submitted a memorial begging to retire; summoned for audience and earnestly urged, he pleaded more firmly and was then appointed Vice Minister of Works and permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he memorialized to retire on account of age; summoned and pressed to stay, he pleaded all the more firmly and was allowed to retire as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遣使就第賜器幣，給全奉，詔本府歲時存問，章奏聽附驛以聞。

translations.literal: The next day an emissary was sent to his residence with vessels and silks, full salary was granted, and an edict ordered the prefecture to inquire after him seasonally; memorials were permitted to be sent via courier relay.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an envoy brought vessels and silks to his home, his full salary was continued, and the prefecture was ordered to visit him each season; his memorials might be sent by post.

sentences.zh: 命其子正辭知公安縣，以便侍養，許歸江陵。

translations.literal: His son Zhengcix was ordered to govern Gong'an County for convenient nursing, and he was permitted to return to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengcix was appointed magistrate of Gong'an to attend him, and he was allowed to return to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 舊制，致仕官止謝殿門外，昂特延見命坐，恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: By old rule, retired officials only thanked outside the hall door; Ang was specially granted an extended audience and a seat—the grace was exceedingly thick.
translations.idiomatic: By custom retired officials bowed only outside the hall; Ang was specially received, given a seat, and honored beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 令俟秋涼上道，遣中使賜宴於玉津園，兩製三館皆預，仍詔賦詩餞行，縉紳榮之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to wait for cool autumn before traveling; a palace attendant was sent to grant a banquet at Yujin Garden, with both academicians and the Three Repositories all in attendance; the court still ordered poems composed to send him off—the officials were honored.
translations.idiomatic: Told to wait for cool autumn before departing, he was feasted at Yujin Garden by imperial envoy, with Hanlin and Three Repositories scholars present; the court ordered farewell poems written—a mark of high honor.

sentences.zh: 昂前後所得奉賜，以三之一購奇書，以諷誦為樂。

translations.literal: Ang used one-third of his salary and gifts to buy rare books and took chanting them as his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He spent a third of his stipends and gifts on rare books and made reciting them his delight.

sentences.zh: 及是閑居，自稱退叟，著《資理論》三卷上之，詔以其書付史館。

translations.literal: At retirement he called himself the "Retired Elder," wrote the "Treatise on Governing Principles" in three scrolls and submitted it; an edict ordered the work sent to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he styled himself the "Retired Elder," wrote a three-scroll "Treatise on Governing Principles," and submitted it; the court ordered it deposited in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 弟協以純謹著稱，仕至主客郎中、雍王府翊善。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xie was known for pure prudence and served to Director of Receiving Guests and Tutor of the Prince of Yong's mansion.
