translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xie, noted for pure and careful conduct, rose to Director of Receiving Guests and Tutor in the Prince of Yong's household.

sentences.zh: 昂以書招之，協亦告老歸。

translations.literal: Ang wrote inviting him, and Xie also retired.
translations.idiomatic: Ang wrote inviting him home, and Xie retired as well.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆眉壽，時人比漢之二疏。

translations.literal: Both brothers lived to great age, and people compared them to the Two Shus of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers lived to ripe old age, and men compared them to the Two Shus of Han.

sentences.zh: 知府陳堯谘署其居曰東、西致政坊。

translations.literal: Prefect Chen Yaozhi named their residences the East and West Retirement Districts.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Chen Yaozhi named their homes the East and West Retirement Quarters.

sentences.zh: 昂於所居建二亭：曰知止，曰幽棲。

translations.literal: At his dwelling Ang built two pavilions, called "Knowing Stop" and "Secluded Dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: At his residence he built two pavilions: "Knowing When to Stop" and "Quiet Retreat."

sentences.zh: 頗好釋氏書。

translations.literal: He quite loved Buddhist books.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of Buddhist writings.

sentences.zh: 晚歲自為墓誌。

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote his own tomb inscription.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he composed his own epitaph.

sentences.zh: 景德四年卒，年八十三，門人諡曰正裕先生。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde he died at age eighty-three; his disciples gave him the posthumous title Master Zhengyu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1007 at eighty-three; his disciples styled him Master Zhengyu.

sentences.zh: 詔加賻贈，錄其孫適出身。

translations.literal: An edict added funeral gifts and enrolled his grandson Shi for initial office entry.
translations.idiomatic: The court added funeral gifts and granted his grandson Shi initial entry into office.

sentences.zh: 昂好學，純厚有清節，澹於榮利，為洗馬十五年，不以屑意。

translations.literal: Ang loved learning, was pure and generous with integrity, and was indifferent to glory and profit; as Grand Mentor for fifteen years he gave it no heed.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, was pure and upright, and cared little for rank or gain; for fifteen years as Grand Mentor he scarcely minded the post.

sentences.zh: 居內署，非公事不至兩府。

translations.literal: In the inner secretariat, unless on public business he did not go to the Two Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner service he visited the Two Offices only on public business.

sentences.zh: 在王邸時，真宗居儲宮，知其素守，故每加褒進，然昂未嘗有所私請，進退存禮，士類多之。

translations.literal: When he was in the prince's household, Zhenzong as heir knew his long-standing conduct and therefore repeatedly praised and promoted him; yet Ang never made private requests, and in advance and withdrawal he preserved propriety—the scholar class greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At the heir's household Zhenzong knew his long integrity and repeatedly favored him, yet Ang never asked private favors; in coming and going he kept the rites, and men of letters admired him.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子正彝、正辭並登進士第，正基虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: His sons Zhengyi and Zhengcix both passed the jinshi examination; Zhengji was Deputy Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhengyi and Zhengcix both passed the jinshi; Zhengji served as Deputy Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 趙鄰幾，字亞之，鄆州須城人，家世為農。

translations.literal: Zhao Linji, styled Yazhi, was a native of Xucheng in Yan Prefecture; his family for generations had been farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Linji, courtesy name Yazhi, was from Xucheng in Yan Prefecture; his family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 鄰幾少好學，能屬文，嘗作《禹別九州賦》，凡萬餘言，人多傳誦。

translations.literal: Linji from youth loved learning and was skilled at prose; he once wrote the "Fu on Yu's Division of the Nine Provinces," more than ten thousand words in all, and many people passed it along and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and wrote well; his "Fu on Yu's Division of the Nine Provinces" ran to more than ten thousand words and was widely copied and recited.

sentences.zh: 周顯德二年舉進士，解褐秘書省校書郎，曆許州、宋州從事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhou Xiande he passed the jinshi examination, entered service as a proofreader of the Secretariat, and served as staff member in Xuzhou and Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 955 he passed the jinshi, entered service as a Secretariat proofreader, and served on the staffs of Xuzhou and Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，召為左讚善大夫、直史館，改宗正丞。

translations.literal: Early in Taiping Xingguo he was summoned as Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent and Concurrent Attendant of the Historiography Institute, then changed to Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he was summoned as Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent with concurrent duty in the Historiography Institute, then made Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 四年，郭贄、宋白授中書舍人，告謝日交薦之，俄而鄰幾獻頌，上覽而嘉之，遷左補闕、知制誥，數月卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Guo Zan and Song Bai were appointed Secretariat Gentlemen; on their thanksgiving day they jointly recommended him; soon Linji submitted an eulogy; the emperor viewed it and praised it; he was transferred to Left Supplementation Censor and Edict Drafter; within a few months he died at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In 979 Guo Zan and Song Bai became Secretariat Gentlemen and recommended him at their thanksgiving audience; Linji soon submitted a eulogy that pleased the emperor, was made Left Supplementation Censor and Edict Drafter, and died within months at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 中使護葬。

translations.literal: A palace attendant escorted the burial.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant supervised his burial.

sentences.zh: 鄰幾體貌尫弱，如不勝衣。

translations.literal: Linji's physique was weak and slender, as if his clothes could scarcely be borne.
translations.idiomatic: He was slight and frail, as though his frame could barely hold his robes.

sentences.zh: 為文浩博，慕徐、庾及王、楊、盧、駱之體，每構思，必斂衽危坐，成千言始下筆。

translations.literal: His writing was vast and abundant; he admired the style of Xu Ling and Yu Xin and of Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo; each time he composed he had to gather his robes and sit upright, and only after a thousand words would take up the brush.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was vast and learned; he admired the styles of Xu Ling, Yu Xin, and the Wang-Yang-Lu-Luo school; before writing he would sit upright with robes gathered, and only after a thousand words in mind would he take up the brush.

sentences.zh: 屬對精切，致意縝密，時輩咸推服之。

translations.literal: His parallel prose was precise, his meaning meticulous, and contemporaries all deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: His parallel prose was exact and his thought dense; contemporaries all bowed to his skill.

sentences.zh: 及掌誥命，頗繁富冗長，不達體要，無稱職之譽。

translations.literal: When he managed edicts his style was quite verbose and long, did not grasp essentials, and won no reputation for competent service.
translations.idiomatic: In drafting edicts he grew florid and long-winded, missed the essential point, and won no praise as a fit drafter.

sentences.zh: 常欲追補唐武宗以來實錄，孜孜訪求遺事，殆廢寢食，會疾革，唯以書未成為恨。

translations.literal: He often wished to supplement the Veritable Records from Tang Wuzong onward, diligently sought out lost affairs, and nearly abandoned sleep and food; when his illness became critical his only regret was that the book was not finished.
translations.idiomatic: He long sought to continue the Tang Veritable Records from Emperor Wuzong onward, hunted lost materials until he nearly forgot sleep and food, and on his deathbed grieved only that the book remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 至淳化中，參知政事蘇易簡因言及鄰幾追補《唐實錄》事，鄰幾一子東之，以蔭補郎山主簿，部送軍糧詣北邊，沒焉，其家屬寄居睢陽。

translations.literal: By the Chunhua period, Vice Grand Councilor Su Yijian mentioned Linji's work on supplementing the Tang Veritable Records; Linji's son Dongzhi, having entered office by yin privilege as chief clerk of Langshan, was escorting military grain to the northern border and perished; his family sojourned in Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunhua years Su Yijian mentioned Linji's unfinished Tang records; Linji's son Dongzhi, a Langshan chief clerk by yin privilege, died escorting grain northward, and the family lodged at Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣直史館錢熙往取其書，得鄰幾所補《會昌以來日曆》二十六卷及文集三十四卷，所著《鯫子》一卷、《六帝年略》一卷、《史氏懋官志》五卷，並他書五十餘卷來上，皆塗竄之筆也。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor sent Historiography Attendant Qian Xi to fetch his books; he obtained Linji's supplemented "Calendar from Huichang Onward" in twenty-six scrolls, collected works in thirty-four scrolls, the "Ziyu" in one scroll, the "Six Emperors' Year Summaries" in one scroll, the "Record of Historiographical Officials" in five scrolls, and more than fifty other scrolls of books submitted—all draft emendation in brush.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Qian Xi to retrieve his papers: twenty-six scrolls of "Calendar from Huichang Onward," thirty-four of collected works, plus "Ziyu," "Six Emperors' Year Summaries," "Record of Historiographical Officials," and fifty-odd other scrolls—all in draft emendation.

sentences.zh: 詔賜其家錢十萬。

translations.literal: An edict granted the family one hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the family one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 時又有何承裕者，晉天福末擢進士第，有清才，好為歌詩，而嗜酒狂逸。

translations.literal: At that time there was also He Chengyu, who at the end of Jin Tianfu passed the jinshi examination; he had pure talent, loved writing poems, and was addicted to wine, wild and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: There was also He Chengyu, who passed the jinshi at the end of the Jin Tianfu era; gifted and poetic, he drank hard and lived without restraint.

sentences.zh: 初為中都主簿，桑維翰鎮兗州，知其直率，不責以吏事。

translations.literal: Initially he was chief clerk of Zhongdu; Sang Weihan governed Yanzhou, knew his frankness, and did not charge him with clerkly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He began as chief clerk of Zhongdu; Sang Weihan, governing Yanzhou, knew his blunt honesty and did not burden him with clerk's work.

sentences.zh: 累官至著作佐郎、直史館，出為盩厔、咸陽二縣令，醉則露首跨牛趨府，府尹王彥超以其名士而容之，然為治清而不煩，民頗安焉。

translations.literal: He rose to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat and Concurrent Attendant of the Historiography Institute, went out as magistrate of Zhouzhi and Xianyang; when drunk he would bare his head and ride an ox to the prefectural office; Prefect Wang Yanchao, as a famous scholar, tolerated him, yet his governance was clear without trouble and the people were quite at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Secretariat Assistant Gentleman with concurrent Historiography duty, then served as magistrate of Zhouzhi and Xianyang; drunk, he would ride an ox bareheaded to the yamen, and Prefect Wang Yanchao, knowing him as a man of letters, indulged him—yet his rule was clear and light, and the people were content.

sentences.zh: 每覽牒訴，必戲判以喻曲直，訴者多心伏引去。

translations.literal: Each time he reviewed petitions he would jestingly judge to clarify right and wrong, and many plaintiffs left secretly convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Reading petitions, he often rendered playful judgments that made the rights and wrongs plain; many litigants withdrew convinced.

sentences.zh: 往往召豪吏接坐，引滿，吏因醉挾私白事，承裕悟之，笑曰：「此見罔也，當受杖。

translations.literal: He often summoned powerful clerks to sit with him and fill their cups; in their drunkenness the clerks would privately tell him affairs; Chengyu perceived it and laughed, saying: "This is deception—you should take the rod."
translations.idiomatic: He would summon powerful clerks to drink with him; when they grew drunk and tried to slip him private business, he would laugh: "That is a trick—you deserve the rod."

sentences.zh: 」杖訖，復召與飲。

translations.literal: When the beating was finished he again summoned them to drink.
translations.idiomatic: When the beating was done he would call them back to drink again.

sentences.zh: 其無檢多類此。

translations.literal: His lack of restraint was mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: His want of restraint was mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，自涇陽令入為監察御史，後曆侍御史，累知忠、萬、商三州，太平興國中卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he entered from magistrate of Jingyang as Investigating Censor, later served as Attendant Censor, successively governed Zhong, Wan, and Shang Prefectures, and died during Taiping Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: In 970 he left the magistracy of Jingyang for Investigating Censor, later Attendant Censor, governed Zhong, Wan, and Shang in turn, and died during Taiping Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 鄭起，字孟隆，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Zheng Qi, styled Menglong—it is not known where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qi, courtesy name Menglong—his birthplace is unknown.

sentences.zh: 少遊京、洛間，佻薄無檢操。

translations.literal: In youth he wandered between the capital and Luoyang, frivolous and without moral restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he wandered between the capital and Luoyang, loose and without self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 聞襄州雙泉寺僧能為黃金，往依焉，遂削髮為侍者。

translations.literal: He heard that a monk at Shuangquan Temple in Xiangzhou could make gold, went to rely on him, and shaved his head to become an attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that a monk at Shuangquan Temple in Xiangzhou could make gold, he went to study with him and shaved his head as a temple attendant.

sentences.zh: 久之，知其誑耀，乃反初服。

translations.literal: After a long time he knew it was fraud and boast, and returned to lay clothing.
translations.idiomatic: After long acquaintance he saw the trick for what it was and returned to lay dress.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，時舉子多尚詩賦，惟起有文七軸，歌詩尤清麗。

translations.literal: He took the jinshi examination; at the time examination candidates mostly prized shi and fu, but Qi alone had seven scrolls of prose, and his songs and poems were especially clear and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He sat for the jinshi when most candidates favored shi and fu; Qi alone submitted seven scrolls of prose, and his lyrics were especially fine.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，調補尉氏主簿，秩滿，以書幹宰相範質，薦為右拾遺、直史館。

translations.literal: Early in Zhou Guangshun he was transferred to supplement chief clerk of Weishi; when his term was finished he approached Chancellor Fan Zhi with a letter and was recommended as Right Reminder and Concurrent Attendant of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he became chief clerk of Weishi; when his term ended he wrote to Chancellor Fan Zhi and was recommended as Right Reminder with concurrent Historiography duty.

sentences.zh: 恭帝初，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Early in the Gongdi reign he was transferred to Attendant Palace Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gongdi he was made Attendant Palace Aide.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，出掌泗州市征。

translations.literal: Early in Qiande he was sent out to manage the market tax of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande he was sent to collect market taxes at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史張延範檢校司徒，官吏呼以「太保」。

translations.literal: The prefect Zhang Yanfan was concurrently honored as Grand Steward, and officials called him "Grand Protector."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Yanfan held the honorary title Grand Steward, and staff addressed him as "Grand Protector."

sentences.zh: 起貧，常乘騾。

translations.literal: Qi was poor and often rode a donkey.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was poor and usually rode a donkey.

sentences.zh: 一日，從延範出近郊送客，延範揖起曰：「請策馬令進。

translations.literal: One day, following Yanfan out to the near suburbs to see off a guest, Yanfan bowed to Qi and said: "Please whip your horse and advance.
translations.idiomatic: One day, seeing a guest off with Yanfan in the suburbs, Yanfan bowed and said: "Pray spur your horse and go ahead.

sentences.zh: 」起曰：「此騾也，不當過呼耳。

translations.literal: " Qi said: "This is a donkey—it should not be addressed too grandly.
translations.idiomatic: " Qi replied: "This is a donkey—it hardly deserves so lofty an address."

sentences.zh: 」以譏延範，延範深銜之，密奏起嗜酒廢職。

translations.literal: " to mock Yanfan; Yanfan deeply resented it and secretly memorialized that Qi was addicted to wine and neglected his duties.
translations.idiomatic: "—a barb aimed at Yanfan, who deeply resented it and secretly reported that Qi drank to excess and neglected his post.

sentences.zh: 初，顯德末，起見太祖握禁兵，有人望，乃上書範質，極言其事。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Xiande, Qi saw that Taizu held command of the forbidden army and enjoyed popular esteem, and therefore submitted a letter to Fan Zhi strongly stating the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiande era Qi saw that Taizu commanded the palace guard and commanded wide respect; he wrote to Fan Zhi urging action on the point.

sentences.zh: 又嘗遇太祖於路，橫絕前導而過，太祖亦弗之怒。

translations.literal: He also once met Taizu on the road, cut across before the escort and passed by, and Taizu likewise did not grow angry.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road he cut in front of Taizu's escort and passed on; the emperor did not take offense.

sentences.zh: 及延範奏至，出為河西令。

translations.literal: When Yanfan's memorial arrived, Qi was sent out as magistrate of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanfan's memorial reached court, Qi was posted out as magistrate of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 會蜀平，當徙遠官，起不欲往，乃炙烙其足，因是成疾而卒。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was to be transferred to a distant post; Qi did not wish to go and therefore cauterized his feet, and on that account fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: With the conquest of Shu he was slated for a distant post; unwilling to go, he burned his feet, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 起負才倨傲，多所詆訐，數為群小窘辱，終亦不改。

translations.literal: Qi relied on his talent and was arrogant, slandered many people, and was repeatedly humiliated by petty men, yet in the end he did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and overbearing, he slandered freely and was often shamed by lesser men—yet he never changed.

sentences.zh: 時有郭昱者，好為古文，狹中詭僻。

translations.literal: At that time there was Guo Yu, who loved to write ancient-style prose, narrow-minded, eccentric, and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Guo Yu, a writer of archaizing prose—narrow, eccentric, and odd.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中登進士第，恥赴常選，獻書於宰相趙普，自比巢、由，朝議惡其矯激，故久不調。

translations.literal: During Zhou Xiande he passed the jinshi examination, was ashamed to attend the regular selection, submitted a letter to Chancellor Zhao Pu comparing himself to Chao Fu and Xu You; court opinion detested his affectation and extravagance, and therefore for long he received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi under Xiande, refused the regular roster, and wrote to Zhao Pu comparing himself to Chao Fu and Xu You; the court disliked his theatrics and long withheld appointment.

sentences.zh: 後復伺普，望塵自陳，普笑謂人曰：「今日甚榮，得巢、由拜於馬首。

translations.literal: Later he again watched for Pu, bowing from the dust to present himself; Pu laughed and said to others: "Today is very glorious—I have Chao and Xu bowing at my horse's head.
translations.idiomatic: Later he waylaid Pu on the road and bowed from the dust; Pu laughed: "What honor—Chao and Xu kowtow at my horse's head.

sentences.zh: 」開寶末，普出鎮河陽，昱詣薛居正上書，極言謗普，居正奏之，詔署襄州觀察推官。

translations.literal: " At the end of Kaibao, when Pu went out to govern Heyang, Yu approached Xue Juzheng and submitted a letter strongly slandering Pu; Juzheng memorialized it, and an edict appointed him Investigating Officer of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " At Kaibao's end, when Pu went to Heyang, Yu denounced him to Xue Juzheng, who memorialized the court; Yu was appointed investigating officer at Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 潘美鎮襄陽，討金陵，以昱隨軍。

translations.literal: Pan Mei governed Xiangyang and campaigned against Jinling; Yu accompanied the army.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei, governing Xiangyang, marched on Jinling with Yu in his train.

sentences.zh: 昱中夜被酒號叫，軍中皆驚，翌日，美遣還。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night Yu, drunk, shouted and cried out, and all in the army were alarmed; the next day Mei sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: One night, drunk, he shouted till the camp was alarmed; Mei sent him home the next day.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，坐盜用官錢除名，因居襄陽，遊索樊、鄧間，雍熙中卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was stripped of office for embezzling official funds, and therefore lived in Xiangyang, wandering and demanding payment between Fan and Deng; he died during Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was cashiered for misusing public funds, lingered in Xiangyang begging between Fan and Deng, and died during Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 又有馬應者，薄有文藝，多服道士衣，自稱「 先生」。

translations.literal: There was also Ma Ying, who had slight literary talent, often wore Daoist robes, and styled himself "Master."
translations.idiomatic: There was also Ma Ying, a minor man of letters who often wore Daoist garb and called himself "Master."

sentences.zh: 開寶初效元結《中興頌》作《勃興頌》，以述太祖下荊、湖之功，欲刊石於永州結《頌》之側，縣令惡其誇誕，不以聞。

translations.literal: Early in Kaibao he modeled Yuan Jie's "Ode on the Restoration" to compose the "Ode on the Surging Rise," describing Taizu's conquest of Jing and Hu; he wished to carve it in stone beside Jie's "Ode" at Yongzhou, but the county magistrate detested its exaggeration and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaibao he modeled Yuan Jie's "Ode on the Restoration" in a "Ode on the Surging Rise" praising Taizu's conquest of Jing and Hu; he wanted it carved beside Jie's stele at Yongzhou, but the magistrate thought it bombastic and suppressed it.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，登第，授大理評事，坐事除名，羈旅積年。

translations.literal: Early in Taiping Xingguo he passed the examination, was appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, was stripped of office for an offense, and wandered as a guest for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he passed the examinations and became a judicial assessor, was dismissed for an offense, and wandered for years.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，以詩幹同年殿中丞牛景，景因奏上，太宗覽而嘉之，復授大理評事，未幾卒。

translations.literal: During Chunhua, with poems he approached his examination-year colleague Palace Aide Niu Jing; Jing therefore memorialized them upward; Taizong viewed them and praised them; he was again appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, and within a short time died.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua he sent poems to his fellow jinshi Niu Jing, who forwarded them; Taizong admired them and restored him as judicial assessor; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 又有穎贄、董淳、劉從義善為文章，張翼、譚用之善為詩，張之翰善箋啟。

translations.literal: There were also Ying Zan, Dong Chun, and Liu Congyi, who were skilled at writing prose; Zhang Yi and Tan Yongzhi, skilled at poetry; and Zhang Zhihan, skilled at letters and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zan, Dong Chun, and Liu Congyi wrote prose; Zhang Yi and Tan Yongzhi wrote poetry; Zhang Zhihan wrote polished memorials.

sentences.zh: 贄拔萃登科，至太子中允。

translations.literal: Zan passed the special selection examination and rose to Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zan passed the special selection and rose to Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 淳為工部員外郎、直史館，奉詔撰《孟昶紀事》。

translations.literal: Chun was Deputy Director of the Ministry of Works and Concurrent Attendant of the Historiography Institute; by edict he compiled the "Record of Meng Chang's Reign."
translations.idiomatic: Chun was Deputy Director of the Ministry of Works with Historiography duty and compiled the "Record of Meng Chang's Reign" by order.

sentences.zh: 從義多藏書，嘗纘長安碑文為《遺風集》二十卷。

translations.literal: Congyi had many books in his collection and once gathered inscriptions from Chang'an steles into the "Collection of Surviving Styles" in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi owned many books and compiled twenty scrolls of Chang'an stele texts as the "Collection of Surviving Styles."

sentences.zh: 餘皆官不達。

translations.literal: The rest all did not attain office.
translations.idiomatic: The others never rose in office.

sentences.zh: 和峴，字晦仁，開封浚儀人。

translations.literal: He Xian, styled Huiren, was a native of Junyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He Xian, courtesy name Huiren, was from Junyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父凝，晉宰相、太子太傅、魯國公。

translations.literal: His father Ning was a Jin chancellor, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning was a Jin chancellor, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 峴生之年，適會凝入翰林、加金紫、知貢舉，凝喜曰：「我平生美事，三者並集，此子宜於我也。

translations.literal: In the year Xian was born, it happened that Ning entered the Hanlin, was granted gold and purple, and oversaw the examinations; Ning rejoiced and said: "The beautiful affairs of my life—these three together—this child should resemble me.
translations.idiomatic: The year Xian was born, Ning entered the Hanlin, received gold and purple, and headed the examinations; he rejoiced: "The three finest things of my life come together—this child will be like me.

sentences.zh: 」因名之曰三美。

translations.literal: " Therefore he named him Sanmei.
translations.idiomatic: " He named him Sanmei—"Three Beauties."

sentences.zh: 七歲，以門蔭為左千牛備身，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At age seven, by yin privilege he was Left Thousand-Bull Guard, and was transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he entered by yin privilege as Left Thousand-Bull Guard, then became a Secretariat assistant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，加朝散階。

translations.literal: Early in Han Qianyou he was given the Dispersed Court rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han Qianyou era he received Dispersed Court rank.

sentences.zh: 十六，登朝為著作郎。

translations.literal: At sixteen he entered court as Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he entered court as a Secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服闋，拜太常丞。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his father; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，授太常博士，從祀南郊，讚導乘輿，進退閑雅。

translations.literal: Early in Jianlong he was appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; following the sacrifice at the Southern Suburb he guided and praised the imperial carriage, advancing and withdrawing with easy grace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianlong he became a Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctor; at the Southern Suburb rites he guided the imperial carriage with polished grace.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂近侍曰：「此誰氏之子，熟於讚相？

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor said to attendants close at hand: "Whose son is this, so skilled at praise and ritual direction?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked his attendants: "Whose son is this, so practiced in ritual praise?

sentences.zh: 」左右即以峴門閥對。

translations.literal: " Those at his side immediately answered with Xian's family background.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered with Xian's lineage.

sentences.zh: 俄拜刑部員外郎兼博士，仍判太常寺。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice concurrently Doctor, and still directed affairs of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and concurrent doctor, still directing the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年十一月甲子，有事於南郊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande, eleventh month, day jiazi, there was a ceremony at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of 963, on day jiazi, the Southern Suburb sacrifice was held.

sentences.zh: 丁丑冬至，有司復請祀昊天上帝，詔峴議其禮，峴以祭義戒於煩數，請罷之。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, the winter solstice, the proper offices again requested sacrifice to the Supreme Lord of Heaven; an edict ordered Xian to discuss the rite; Xian, because the "Doctrine of Sacrifice" warns against excessive frequency, requested that it be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice on dingchou the offices again proposed sacrifice to Heaven; Xian, citing the "Doctrine of Sacrifice" against excessive rites, urged cancellation.

sentences.zh: 二年，議孝明、孝惠二後神主祔於別廟，峴以舊禮有二後同廟之文，無各殿異室之說，今二後同祔別廟，亦宜共殿別室。

translations.literal: In the second year, when discussing enshrining the spirit tablets of Empresses Xiaoming and Xiaohui in a separate temple, Xian said that old rites had text on two empresses sharing one temple but no statement on separate halls in different chambers; now that the two empresses were jointly enshrined in a separate temple, they should also share one hall with separate chambers.
translations.idiomatic: In 964, debating the separate temple for Empresses Xiaoming and Xiaohui, Xian argued that old rites allowed two empresses one temple but not separate halls—so they should share one hall with separate chambers.

sentences.zh: 孝明皇后嘗母儀天下，宜居上室。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoming had once been mother to all under Heaven and should occupy the upper chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoming had once been mother of the realm and should take the upper chamber.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇后止以追尊，當居次室。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaohui had only posthumous elevation and should occupy the secondary chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaohui, honored only posthumously, should take the lower chamber.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 三年春，初克夔州，以內衣庫使李光睿權知州，峴通判州事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, when Kuizhou was first taken, the Inner Garment Store envoy Li Guangrui was appointed acting governor; Xian served as judicial commissioner of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 965, when Kuizhou fell, Li Guangrui was acting governor and Xian served as judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 代還，是歲十二月十四日戊戌臘，有司以七日辛卯蠟百神，峴獻議正之。

translations.literal: When he returned from replacement duty, that year on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, day wuxu, the wax month, the proper offices scheduled the wax sacrifice to the hundred spirits on the seventh day, day xinmao; Xian submitted a memorial to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Returning that year, on the fourteenth of the twelfth month (wuxu) he corrected the schedule when the offices set the wax rites for the seventh (xinmao).

sentences.zh: 四年，南郊，峴建議望燎位置爟火。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at the Southern Suburb, Xian proposed placing the signal fire for the gazing-at-blaze rite.
translations.idiomatic: In 966, at the Southern Suburb, he proposed the placement of the signal fire for the blaze-gazing rite.

sentences.zh: 又嘗言：「依舊典，宗廟殿庭設宮縣三十六架，加鼓吹熊羆十二案，朝會登歌用五瑞，郊廟奠獻用四瑞，回仗至樓前奏《采茨之曲》，禦樓奏《隆安之曲》，各用樂章。

translations.literal: He also once said: "According to old canon, in the ancestral temple hall and court were set palace bells in thirty-six frames, with twelve tables of drum-and-bear music added; at court assemblies the ascending song used the Five Auspicious Objects; at suburban temples the offering used the Four Auspicious Objects; when the returning escort reached before the tower the "Song of Cai Ci" was played; at the imperial tower the "Song of Long An" was played—each with its musical chapter.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged restoring old practice: thirty-six palace bell frames in the ancestral temple, twelve drum-and-bear tables, the Five Auspicious Objects for court song, the Four for suburban offerings, "Cai Ci" before the tower, "Long An" at the imperial tower—each with its proper movement.

sentences.zh: 」復舉唐故事，宗廟祭科處別設珍膳，用申孝享之意。

translations.literal: " He again cited Tang precedent that at ancestral sacrifices a separate table of delicacies should be set to express filial intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He cited Tang precedent for separate delicacies at ancestral rites to express filial intent.

sentences.zh: 又謂「《八佾》之舞以象文德武功，請用《玄德升聞》、《天下大定》二舞」。

translations.literal: He also said: "The dance of eight rows represents civil and martial virtue; I request using the two dances 'Mysterious Virtue Ascending in Fame' and 'All Under Heaven Greatly Settled.'"
translations.idiomatic: He proposed the eight-row dance symbolizing civil and martial virtue, using "Mysterious Virtue Ascending in Fame" and "All Under Heaven Greatly Settled."

sentences.zh: 並從其議。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 事具《禮》、《樂志》。

translations.literal: The matters are detailed in the "Rites" and "Music" treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in the "Rites" and "Music" treatises.

sentences.zh: 先是，王樸、竇儼洞曉音樂，前代不協律呂者多所考正。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Pu and Dou Yi thoroughly understood music, and many pieces from former ages that did not accord with pitch and mode they largely examined and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu and Dou Yi had mastered music and corrected much that failed to match proper pitch.

sentences.zh: 樸、儼既沒，未有繼其職者。

translations.literal: After Pu and Yi died, there was no one to succeed to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: After their deaths no one succeeded them.

sentences.zh: 會太祖以雅樂聲高，詔峴講求其理，以均節之，自是八音和暢，上甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When Taizu found the court music's pitch too high, he ordered Xian to investigate the principle and regulate it evenly; from this the eight tones harmonized smoothly, and the emperor greatly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Finding court pitch too high, Taizu had Xian investigate and regulate it; the eight tones harmonized, and the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 語具《律志》。

translations.literal: The discussion is detailed in the "Treatise on Pitch."
translations.idiomatic: The account is in the "Treatise on Pitch."

sentences.zh: 樂器中有叉手笛者，上意欲增入雅樂，峴即令樂工調品，以諧律呂，其執持之狀如拱揖然，請目曰「拱辰管」，詔備於樂府。

translations.literal: Among the instruments was one called the crossed-hand flute; the emperor wished to add it to court music; Xian immediately ordered the musicians to adjust its pitch to harmonize with modes; its held posture was like bowing in salute, and he requested it be titled the "Bow-to-the-Constellations Pipe"; an edict ordered it prepared in the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu wished to add the crossed-hand flute to court music, Xian tuned it to the modes; held like a bow, it was named the "Bow-to-the-Constellations Pipe" and entered the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 峴性苛刻鄙吝，好殖財，復輕侮人，嘗以官船載私貨販易規利。

translations.literal: Xian by nature was harsh, mean, and stingy, loved amassing wealth, and again lightly insulted people; he once used an official boat to carry private goods to trade for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh, stingy, and greedy, he often insulted others and once used an official boat to trade private goods for profit.

sentences.zh: 初為判官鄭同度論奏，既而彰信軍節度劉遇亦上言，按得實，坐削籍，配隸汝州。

translations.literal: Initially investigating officer Zheng Tong memorialized against him; soon Military Commissioner Liu Yu of Zhangxin Army also submitted a report; investigation found it true, and he was demoted from the register and assigned to serve at Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Investigator Zheng Tong memorialized against him; Liu Yu of Zhangxin Army confirmed it; Xian was struck from the rolls and assigned to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，起為太常丞，分司西京，復階勳章服。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was restored as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, serving as commissioner at the Western Capital, and his rank, merit insignia, and robes were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 969 he was restored as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at the Western Capital, with rank and insignia returned.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，上躬耕籍田，峴奉留司賀表至闕下，因以其所著《奉常集》五卷、《秘閣集》二十卷、《注釋武成王廟讚》五卷奏禦，上甚嘉之，復授主客郎中，判太常寺兼禮儀院事。

translations.literal: Early in Duangong, when the emperor personally plowed the sacred field, Xian's congratulatory memorial as left-behind official reached the palace; he therefore submitted to the throne his "Collection of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices" in five scrolls, "Secret Archive Collection" in twenty scrolls, and "Annotated Eulogies of the Temple of King Wucheng" in five scrolls; the emperor greatly praised them and again appointed him Director of Receiving Guests, directing the Court of Imperial Sacrifices concurrently with the Ritual Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong, when Taizong plowed the sacred field, Xian's congratulatory memorial arrived with his five-scroll "Collection of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices," twenty-scroll "Secret Archive Collection," and five-scroll "Annotated Eulogies of the Temple of King Wucheng"; he was restored as Director of Receiving Guests with charge of ritual affairs.

sentences.zh: 是秋得暴疾，卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: That autumn he suffered a sudden illness and died at age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died suddenly at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 弟蒙。

translations.literal: Younger brother Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Meng.

sentences.zh: 蒙字顯仁，凝第四子也。

translations.literal: Meng, styled Xianren, was Ning's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, courtesy name Xianren, was Ning's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 生五六歲，凝教之誦古詩賦，一曆輒不忘。

translations.literal: When he was five or six, Ning taught him to recite ancient poems and fu, and once through he did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: At five or six Ning taught him poems and fu; one reading and he remembered.

sentences.zh: 試令詠物為四句詩，頗有思致，凝歎賞而奇之，語峴曰：「此兒他日必以文章顯，吾老矣，不見，汝曹善保護之。」

translations.literal: Testing him with four-line poems on objects, he showed considerable thought; Ning sighed in admiration and marveled at him, saying to Xian: "This boy will surely become famous through writing; I am old and will not see it—you must protect him well."
translations.idiomatic: Asked for quatrains on objects, he showed real wit; Ning marveled and told Xian: "This child will distinguish himself by writing; I am old and will not see it—you must guard him well."

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年擢進士第，釋褐霍丘主簿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and upon leaving the common cloth was appointed chief clerk of Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In 983 he passed the jinshi and became chief clerk of Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，知崇仁縣，就拜大理評事。

translations.literal: Early in Yongxi he governed Chongren County and was thereupon appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi he governed Chongren and was made a judicial assessor.

sentences.zh: 江南轉運楊緘以其材幹奏，移知南昌縣。

translations.literal: Jiangnan Transport Commissioner Yang Jian memorialized his competence and ability, and he was transferred to govern Nanchang County.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Yang Jian recommended his ability and moved him to magistrate of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 代還，刑部取為詳覆官，遷光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: When he returned from replacement duty, the Ministry of Justice took him as detailed review officer, and he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: On return the Ministry of Justice made him a detailed review officer, then Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 先是，凝嘗取古今史傳聽訟斷獄、辨雪冤枉等事著為《疑獄集》，蒙因增益事類，分為三卷，表上之。

translations.literal: Earlier Ning had taken from ancient and modern histories cases of hearing lawsuits, judging crimes, and clearing wrongful accusations and compiled the "Collection of Doubtful Cases"; Meng added categories of affairs, divided it into three scrolls, and submitted it in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Ning had compiled the "Collection of Doubtful Cases" from historical trials; Meng expanded it to three scrolls and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 俄獻所著文賦五十軸，召試中書，擢為太子中允。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted fifty scrolls of his writings and fu; summoned for examination at the Secretariat, he was promoted to Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted fifty scrolls of prose and fu, passed a Secretariat examination, and became Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 先是，馮起撰《御前登第三榜碑》以獻，上甚稱獎，命直史館。

translations.literal: Earlier Feng Qi had compiled the "Stele of the Third Rank before the Throne" and submitted it; the emperor greatly praised it and ordered him Concurrent Attendant of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Feng Qi had submitted the "Stele of the Third Rank before the Throne" and won high praise and Historiography duty.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，蒙又撰《七榜題名記》，並補注凝所撰《古今孝悌集成》十卷以獻，遂以本官直集賢院，中謝日，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Early in Chunhua, Meng again compiled the "Record of the Seven Examination Lists" and supplemented Ning's "Comprehensive Collection of Filial Piety and Fraternal Duty, Ancient and Modern" in ten scrolls and submitted them; he was therefore with his original office made Concurrent Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and on the day of mid-audience thanks was granted the red robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunhua Meng submitted the "Record of the Seven Examination Lists" and a supplemented ten-scroll "Comprehensive Collection of Filial Piety and Fraternal Duty"; he entered the Hall of Assembled Worthies and received the red robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 三年春，獻《觀燈賦》，詔付史館，遷右正言。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he submitted the "Fu on Viewing the Lanterns"; an edict ordered it sent to the Historiography Institute, and he was transferred to Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third Chunhua year he submitted a "Fu on Viewing the Lanterns"; the court sent it to the Historiography Institute and made him Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太宗親試貢士，蒙預考校，作歌以獻，上對宰相稱賞之，召問年幾何。

translations.literal: That year Taizong personally tested examination candidates; Meng participated in grading and composed a song to submit; the emperor spoke to the chancellor in praise of it and summoned him to ask his age.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taizong personally examined candidates; Meng helped grade, submitted a song, and the emperor praised him to the chancellor and asked his age.

sentences.zh: 時摹印《儒行篇》，以賜新及第人及三館、台省官，皆上表稱謝。

translations.literal: At that time block-printed copies of the "Chapter on the Scholar's Conduct" were given to new jinshi and to officials of the Three Repositories and the Secretariat and Censorate—all submitted memorials of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Block prints of the "Chapter on the Scholar's Conduct" were given to new jinshi and Three Repositories and Secretariat-Censorate officials, who all submitted thanks.

sentences.zh: 上時禦便坐，出表以示宰相，而蒙洎尤稱上旨，因謂李昉曰：「蒙，宰相子，勤學自立，有文章，能荷堂構，如蒙者不可多得也。

translations.literal: The emperor at the time was at the informal seat and produced the memorials to show the chancellor; Meng and Ji especially matched the emperor's intent, and therefore he said to Li Fang: "Meng is a chancellor's son, diligent in learning and self-reliant, with writing; he can bear the hall and roof-beams—men like Meng cannot be obtained in many numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At the informal seat the emperor showed the chancellor the thanks memorials; Meng and Ji pleased him most, and he told Li Fang: "Meng, a chancellor's son, studies hard and writes well—he can bear the family roof; such men are rare.

sentences.zh: 」遂以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon with his original office made Edict Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Edict Drafter at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 不逾年，加水部員外郎、知理檢院。

translations.literal: Within a year he was given the additional title of Deputy Director of the Ministry of Waterways and charge of the Inspection Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was also Deputy Director of the Ministry of Waterways with charge of the Inspection Institute.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，賜金紫，與王旦同判吏部銓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao he was granted gold and purple and together with Wang Dan jointly judged the Ministry of the Civil Office selection.
translations.idiomatic: In 995 he received gold and purple and jointly judged civil appointments with Wang Dan.

sentences.zh: 是秋，晨起將朝，風眩暴作而卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: That autumn, rising early to attend court, he suffered a sudden attack of wind dizziness and died at age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, rising for court, he was struck by vertigo and died at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 上聞之驚歎，遣中使就家問疾狀，並恤其孤，賵賻加等。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he sighed in astonishment, sent a palace attendant to his home to inquire into the illness, and consoled his orphans; funeral gifts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, sent an envoy to inquire, consoled his orphans, and increased funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 長子珙才十歲，即授大理評事。

translations.literal: The eldest son Gong was only ten years old and was immediately appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Gong, only ten, was at once made a judicial assessor.

sentences.zh: 次子敫，補太廟齋郎。

translations.literal: The second son Jiao was appointed Supplementary Officer of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jiao was made Supplementary Officer of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 蒙好修飾容儀，自五鼓張燈燭至辨色，冠帶方畢。

translations.literal: Meng loved to adorn his appearance; from the fifth watch he lit lamps and candles until daybreak, when his cap and belt were finally complete.
translations.idiomatic: Meng loved fine dress; from the fifth watch he lit lamps until dawn before his cap and belt were complete.

sentences.zh: 雖幼能屬文，殊少警策。

translations.literal: Although from youth he could compose prose, he had very little sharp brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Though he could write from youth, his work lacked edge.

sentences.zh: 每草制，必精思討索而後成，拘於引類偶對，頗失典誥之體。

translations.literal: Each time he drafted an edict he had to ponder and search exhaustively before completing it; constrained by parallel categories and couplets, he quite lost the style of canonical proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: Each edict required exhaustive drafting; bound to parallel phrasing, he lost the tone of great proclamations.

sentences.zh: 上以其貴家子，能業文，甚寵待之，欲召入翰林，謂近臣曰：「蒙眸子毛毛然，胸中必不正，不可以居近侍也。

translations.literal: Because he was the son of a noble house and could pursue letters, the emperor greatly favored him and wished to summon him into the Hanlin; he said to close ministers: "Meng's pupils are fuzzy; in his bosom he surely is not upright—he cannot dwell in close attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him as a noble scion and meant to summon him to the Hanlin, but told close ministers: "Meng's eyes are dull; his heart is not straight—he must not serve in close attendance.

sentences.zh: 」其命遂寢。

translations.literal: " The appointment was therefore shelved.
translations.idiomatic: " The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 蒙弟嵲始為三班奉職，淳化中，獻文求試，上以故相之後，改授大理評事。

translations.literal: Meng's younger brother E began as Third-Rank Attendant; during Chunhua he submitted writings requesting trial examination; because he was the descendant of a former chancellor, he was changed and appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother E began as Third-Rank Attendant; in Chunhua he submitted writings for examination and, as a former chancellor's descendant, became a judicial assessor.

sentences.zh: 馮吉，字惟一，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Feng Ji, styled Weiyi, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ji, courtesy name Weiyi, was from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父道，周太師、中書令，追封瀛王。

translations.literal: His father Dao was Zhou Grand Preceptor and Grand Councilor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dao was Zhou Grand Preceptor and Grand Councilor, posthumously Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 吉，晉天福初以父任秘書省校書郎，遷膳部、金部、職方員外郎，屯田、戶部、司勳郎中，累階金紫。

translations.literal: Ji, early in Jin Tianfu by his father's position was Proofreader of the Secretariat, transferred to Deputy Director in the Ministries of Provisions, Treasury, and Bureau of Appointments, Director in the Ministries of Garrison Lands, Revenue, and Merits, and cumulatively rose to gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin Tianfu Ji entered as a Secretariat proofreader by his father's rank, rose through ministries to gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: During Zhou Xiande he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Xiande he became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 吉嗜學，善屬文，工草隸，議者以掌誥許之。

translations.literal: Ji loved learning, was skilled at prose, and excelled at cursive and clerical script; critics agreed he was fit to manage edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, wrote well, and excelled at cursive and clerical script; critics said he was fit to draft edicts.

sentences.zh: 然性滑稽無操行，每中書舍人缺，宰相即欲用吉，終以佻薄而止。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was comic and without moral conduct; each time the Secretariat Gentleman post was vacant the chancellor wished to use Ji, but in the end because he was frivolous it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was comic and unrestrained; whenever the Secretariat Gentleman post opened the chancellor wanted him, but his levity always blocked it.

sentences.zh: 雅好琵琶，尤臻其妙，教坊供奉號名手者亦莫能及。

translations.literal: He deeply loved the pipa and especially reached its subtlety; even famous hands among the Music Office performers could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: He adored the pipa and mastered it beyond even the Music Office's best players.

sentences.zh: 父常戒令勿習，吉性所好，亦不能改。

translations.literal: His father often admonished him not to practice it, but what Ji's nature loved he could not change.
translations.idiomatic: His father forbade it, but nature he could not change.

sentences.zh: 道欲辱之，因家宴，令吉奏琵琶為壽，賜以束帛，吉置於肩，左抱琵琶，按膝再拜如伶官狀，了無怍色，家人皆大笑。

translations.literal: Dao wished to humiliate him and therefore at a family feast ordered Ji to play the pipa for longevity; bestowing silks, Ji placed them on his shoulder, held the pipa in his left arm, pressed his knee and bowed twice in the manner of a performer, with not the least sign of shame; all in the family laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Dao once tried to shame him at a feast, ordering him to play for longevity and giving silks; Ji slung the gift on his shoulder, hugged the pipa, bowed twice like a performer without a blush—and the household roared.

sentences.zh: 及為少卿，頗不得意，以杯酒自娛。

translations.literal: When he became Vice Director he was quite discontent, and consoled himself with cups of wine.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Director he was discontent and drowned his mood in wine.

sentences.zh: 每朝士宴集，雖不召，亦常自至，酒酣即彈琵琶，彈罷賦詩，詩成起舞。

translations.literal: Whenever court officials held feasts, even if he was not summoned he often came of himself; when the wine was warm he would play the pipa, and when the playing finished compose a poem, and when the poem was finished begin to dance.
translations.idiomatic: At officials' feasts, invited or not, he came; warmed with wine he played pipa, then recited a poem, then danced.

sentences.zh: 時人愛其俊逸，謂之「三絕」。

translations.literal: People of the time loved his elegant abandon and called it the "Three Perfections."
translations.idiomatic: Men of the age loved his dash and called it the "Three Perfections."

sentences.zh: 宋初，受詔撰述《明憲皇太后諡議》，見稱於時。

translations.literal: Early in Song, by edict he compiled the "Posthumous Address for Empress Dowager Mingxian" and was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he drafted the "Posthumous Address for Empress Dowager Mingxian" and was praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong he died, age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Jianlong, at the age of forty-five.
